title: Per-account profiles & trade groups
body:
## Context
E28 is the second epic of the **R3 "Trading on demo"** train (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7, sprints S15-S16, 2027-01-01 -> 2027-01-14). It sits on the train's safety scaffolding path: the roadmap's key dates record 2027-01-07 as "Key vault + profiles + risk caps + kill-switch complete - **safety scaffolding lands before the first order ticket ships**", and the dependency graph records `E27 --> E28 --> E34`.

The epic answers one question: **when one intent is executed across several accounts, what decides the size, the leverage, the stop and whether the order is permitted at all?** The answer is the per-account profile, and it is server-side and non-negotiable (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2: "Risk caps are **server-side and non-negotiable** - a manager cannot exceed them from the UI, an API call, or a rule"). Everything downstream depends on it: the order ticket (E30), the fan-out engine (E34), the rule engine (E35), risk lockouts (E39) and journal attribution (E41) all consume the profile, the sizer or the trade group defined here.

The roadmap's scope line for this epic reads: "Profile schema: leverage, sizing rule (% equity / fixed $ / fixed qty / risk-based), SL/TP offsets, max risk per day, max position size, allowed symbols, position mode (one-way/hedge) and margin mode; profile CRUD with validation against instruments-info precision filters; trade-group definition (named set of accounts) with per-account enable/disable; per-trade override semantics documented and enforced; profile simulation preview ('this ticket would place X on A, Y on B')."

Web app only; Bybit USDT linear perpetuals only; the admin surfaces are RBAC-gated screens **inside the web app** - there is no separate admin application (owner decision, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).

## Goal
Make per-account risk policy a first-class, versioned, server-enforced object, and make a named set of accounts a first-class tradable unit - so that a single intent resolves into correctly-sized, correctly-protected, correctly-permitted per-account orders, and so that no client, rule or crafted request can produce an order larger, more levered or less protected than the owner's policy allows.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (domain PROF, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` SS3):**
- **US-PROF-001** Define a per-account profile (Must) - E28-T01, E28-T02, E28-S01
- **US-PROF-002** Sizing rules (Must) - E28-T03, E28-S01
- **US-PROF-003** Allowed-symbol restriction (Must) - E28-T04, E28-S02
- **US-PROF-004** Risk caps enforced server-side (Must) - E28-T04
- **US-PROF-005** Create a trade group (Must) - E28-T05, E28-S03
- **US-PROF-006** Fan-out an order to a trade group (Must) - **preview and sizing only** here (E28-T03, E28-T05, E28-S04); submission, the rate-limit governor and partial-failure remediation are **E34**
- **US-PROF-007** Trade-group lifecycle view (Must) - **definition, listing and read projection** here (E28-T05, E28-S03); the live aggregate view over open positions is completed by **E34** and **E41**
- **US-PROF-008** Per-trade profile overrides (Should) - E28-K01, E28-S05

**Screens:** SCR-130 Admin: per-account profiles list, SCR-131 Admin: profile editor, SCR-132 Admin: profile templates, SCR-133 Admin: symbol permissions matrix, SCR-062 Trade-group manager, and the **preview half** of SCR-061 Trade-group ticket. SCR-114 Trading defaults is touched for the profile-ceiling display.

**Components:** CMP-001, CMP-005, CMP-011, CMP-040, CMP-041, CMP-044, CMP-049, CMP-050, CMP-055, CMP-065, CMP-075, CMP-086, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-100, CMP-101, CMP-102, CMP-104, CMP-105, CMP-106, CMP-107, CMP-119, CMP-121, CMP-123, CMP-124, CMP-138, CMP-158, CMP-229, CMP-231, CMP-232.

**API:** `GET`/`POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles/{profileId}`, `GET`/`POST /trade-groups`, `GET /trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}`, `POST /trade-groups/preview`. `POST /trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend` and `/cancel` are defined in the contract and implemented by **E34**.

**WS:** the `trade_groups` private topic (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS15.5, 100 ms throttle, `orders:read` + granted accounts) - read projection here, live fan-out state in E34.

**DB:** `account_profiles` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4), `trade_groups` (SS3.3.2), `trade_group_legs` (SS3.3.3), plus the `account_profile_revisions` projection this epic adds for versioning.

**Architecture module:** **M13** (fan-out / profile application), with `Sizer`, `ProfileAdmin` and `TradeGroupFanout` from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3.5 and SS10.2.

## Out of scope
- Fan-out **submission**, the per-UID rate-limit governor, partial-failure remediation and unwind - **E34**.
- Order placement, the order state machine and reconciliation - **E29**; the order ticket UI - **E30**.
- The native-SL invariant's enforcement at the OMS acknowledgement boundary - **E32** (this epic guarantees the profile can never *lack* a stop definition; E32 guarantees the order never *reaches the exchange* without one).
- The lockout state machine, its 2FA-gated reset and the kill-switch - **E39** (this epic's guard detects a breach and delegates).
- Rule-engine interaction with profiles - **E35**; journal analytics over overrides and groups - **E41**; the users/roles/audit admin surfaces - **E42**.
- Accounts, sub-accounts and API keys - **E27**. Android, a separate admin app, and any non-Bybit or non-USDT-perp instrument - out of scope for the whole plan.

## Exit criteria
1. Every Must story in the PROF domain is Done, and US-PROF-006 and US-PROF-007 are Done to their E28 boundary with the remainder explicitly carried by E34.
2. A profile cannot be stored, by any path, with `require_native_sl` false - proven at the database, the API and the UI, and drilled in E28-X04.
3. The sizing algorithm produces byte-identical results to the frozen golden vectors, and ten of those vectors are independently recomputed by QA from the story text and match.
4. A preview across five accounts resolves each leg by its own profile, reports every skip with a reason, and returns within 300 ms p95.
5. The risk guard adds <=5 ms p95 to the order path, refuses a crafted non-allowed-symbol order with 403 plus an audit row, and fails **closed** when its inputs are unavailable.
6. A breached cap survives a process restart, a WS reconnect and a clock change (E28-Q03 chaos scenarios 1-3, E28-X04 drill 3).
7. No override can widen any hard cap, by UI or by crafted payload - every protected field asserted individually.
8. RBAC matrix green across every E28 route and the `trade_groups` topic x every role, asserting 403, no state change and an audit row for every disallowed cell (R3 exit criterion #10 for this epic's surface).
9. Design-QA passed on all six surfaces; axe-core clean and manual screen-reader passes done; every status expressed as text.
10. Coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and the group planner, >=80% frontend; zero open P0/P1 against E28's scope; QA and Security sign-offs recorded; demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review.

## Risks
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| A sizing bug produces wrongly-sized orders on N accounts simultaneously | Direct financial loss, multiplied by the group size | Frozen golden vectors, QA's independent recomputation from the story text, property tests asserting realised risk <= budgeted risk, and a regression pack tagged to run on every consuming epic's changes |
| A consumer (E30, E34, E35) re-derives size instead of calling the sizer | Two sources of truth, divergence discovered in production | Single-entry-point rule documented in E28-T06, enforced by the call-site review in E28-X02 |
| The risk guard's in-memory counters desynchronise and reopen a breached cap | A locked-out account trades again | Rebuild from Postgres on start and reconnect, fail-closed on unavailable inputs, chaos scenarios 1-3 and drill 3 |
| Override semantics were left open by the owner decision | Late rework of E30 and E34 | E28-K01 timeboxed to 2 days with the safety floor fixed in advance and ADR-0016 recorded regardless of outcome |
| Profile propagation has no WS topic and the protocol is frozen for R3 | Stale profiles used for sizing in an open ticket | E28-K01 decides the transport with a stated fallback (event-triggered REST re-fetch) that needs no protocol change |
| The symbol matrix at ~400 symbols x N accounts is slow or inaccessible | An unusable admin screen, an a11y gate failure | Virtualisation designed in at E28-D02/D03, the DOM approach decided in E28-D05, budgets asserted in E28-Q04 |
| E28 and E34 both draw SCR-061 | Duplicated or conflicting design | Explicit split recorded in E28-D02's scope: E28 owns the preview, E34 owns send and failure states |

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Policy decides size, not the client
  Given three accounts with different profiles in one trade group
  When one intent is previewed
  Then each account resolves its own quantity, leverage and stop from its own profile, and a client-supplied size is only ever a hint that the server clamps

Scenario: The safety invariant is unbreakable
  When any path - UI, API, template, override or a direct database write - attempts to produce a profile without a mandatory native stop-loss
  Then it is refused, and the refusal is audited

Scenario: Limits survive a hostile client
  When crafted requests attempt a non-allowed symbol, an oversized quantity, a widened cap and an ungranted account
  Then each is refused with the documented code, no state changes, no exchange call is made, and every attempt leaves an audit row

Scenario: The epic's contract holds for its consumers
  Given the order ticket, the fan-out engine and the rule engine all size an identical intent
  Then all three produce the same quantity, because all three call the one sizer
```

## Technical notes / design
The epic is built in strict dependency order: schema (E28-T01) -> contract (E28-T02) -> arithmetic (E28-T03) -> enforcement (E28-T04) -> aggregation (E28-T05), with the UI following two sprints behind its design. The one architectural rule that governs every child is **single authority**: exactly one implementation of sizing (`size_leg`, E28-T03), one of cap enforcement (`guard.check`, E28-T04) and one of group planning (`plan_group`, E28-T05). Consumers - E30, E34, E35 - call them; no consumer re-derives a quantity or re-implements a cap, and the call-site review in E28-X02 enforces it.

The second rule is **the client is never the authority**. Every number the UI computes (the worked example in SCR-131, the send-blocking predicate in SCR-061) exists for latency only and is re-derived server-side; the single permitted duplication, the TypeScript sizing port behind the worked example, is validated against the backend golden vectors in CI so drift fails the build.

The third rule is **fail closed**. Where an input is unavailable - the instrument cache during a save, the position snapshot during a guard evaluation - the operation is refused with a documented code and an alert, never permitted on an assumption.

Money and quantity are `Decimal` end to end (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` invariant C3); no float touches any value that becomes an order, a journal entry or an audit row.

## Test plan
Per-child plans roll up into **E28-Q05**. Layers: unit and property tests on the sizer and the guard (>=90% coverage); contract tests against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the `trade_groups` WS schema; integration against a seeded Postgres with recorded Bybit `instruments-info` fixtures; Playwright E2E across the six surfaces in browser and Electron (**E28-Q02**); k6/Locust load plus five chaos scenarios (**E28-Q03**); axe-core plus manual screen-reader and keyboard passes (**E28-Q04**); RBAC matrix and ten abuse cases as a required CI check (**E28-X03**); manual privilege-escalation and cap-bypass drills (**E28-X04**).

## Security notes
Assets **A-08** (per-account profiles) and **A-09** (trade-group configuration) from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SS4, both integrity-3. Threats owned by this epic: **O3** tampering with size/leverage beyond caps (High), **F2** a profile ignored so one account gets another's sizing (High), **F6** a leg without a native SL because the profile lacked offsets (High), and the repudiation risk **F4** for group actions. Controls implemented: **SR-025** step-up on every profile and cap change, **SR-052** server-side authority over sizing and caps, **SR-053** hard ceilings, **SR-054** allowed-symbol allow-list, **SR-056** the native-SL invariant at the profile layer, **SR-064** audit of every change and refusal, **SR-072** per-leg status recording. STRIDE model in **E28-X01**, review in **E28-X02**, automation in **E28-X03**, drills and sign-off in **E28-X04**. Data classification: Confidential throughout; no secret material ever enters a profile, a snapshot or an API response, proven by test.

## Accessibility notes
Six net-new or changed surfaces, all WCAG 2.2 AA. The epic's binding rules, taken from the screen catalogue: every status is text, never colour alone (SCR-062, SCR-061); matrix cells are checkboxes whose accessible names combine account and symbol (SCR-133); every profile field carries units and a worked example (SCR-131); disabled controls state their reason in visible text (SCR-061, E28-S05's "capped by profile"); live-updating surfaces announce a bounded summary and never steal focus. Design-time review in **E28-D05**, built-code audit in **E28-Q04**, conformance in **E28-D07**.

## Performance notes
Budgets owned by this epic: risk-guard evaluation <=5 ms p95 added to the order path (US-PROF-004); fan-out preview <=300 ms p95 at five accounts (SCR-061); profile save <=2 s including exchange-limit revalidation (SCR-131); symbol matrix render <=600 ms at ~400 symbols (SCR-133); group grid <=4 ms scripting per frame at 50 groups x 5 legs (SCR-062); profile-change propagation to open tickets <=2 s (SCR-130); and a contribution to the fan-out overhead budget of <=50 ms + <=10 ms per additional account p95 (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` SS5.2). Measured and recorded in **E28-Q03**.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_profile_saves_total`, `cv_profile_validation_failures_total`, `cv_profile_save_seconds`, `cv_profile_cache_hit_ratio`, `cv_sizer_duration_seconds`, `cv_sizer_outcomes_total`, `cv_sizer_clamped_total`, `cv_risk_guard_seconds`, `cv_risk_guard_refusals_total`, `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total`, `cv_tradegroup_preview_seconds`, `cv_tradegroup_legs_skipped_total`, `cv_override_applied_total`, `cv_override_clamped_total`.

Alerts: any `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total` increment pages the owner; a cap breach raises a warning notification.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Land account_profiles, trade_groups and trade_group_legs migrations and domain models
body:
## Context
E28 is the second epic of the R3 "Trading on demo" train (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7, S15-S16, 2027-01-01 -> 2027-01-14). Its roadmap scope line reads: "Profile schema: leverage, sizing rule (% equity / fixed $ / fixed qty / risk-based), SL/TP offsets, max risk per day, max position size, allowed symbols, position mode (one-way/hedge) and margin mode; profile CRUD with validation against instruments-info precision filters; trade-group definition (named set of accounts) with per-account enable/disable; per-trade override semantics documented and enforced; profile simulation preview".

Nothing else in the epic can start until the persistence layer exists, because every other ticket - sizing (E28-T03), risk guards (E28-T04), the profile editor (E28-S01) and the group manager (E28-S03) - reads or writes these tables. The DDL is already fully specified in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4 (`account_profiles`), SS3.3.2 (`trade_groups`) and SS3.3.3 (`trade_group_legs`); this Task lands it verbatim with the Alembic migration, the SQLAlchemy models and the Pydantic domain models from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.1 and SS9.2.

The single most important line in the DDL is `CONSTRAINT ap_native_sl CHECK (require_native_sl = true)` - the database itself refuses to store a profile that disables the native stop-loss invariant (owner decision, cross-cutting consequence #3, ADR-0008). That check is not negotiable and must not be relaxed by any later migration.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating `account_profiles` exactly as specified in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4, including every CHECK constraint: `ap_leverage`, `ap_native_sl`, `ap_tif`, `ap_slip`, `ap_opm`, `ap_sl_pos`, `ap_tp_pair`, `ap_tp_pos`, `ap_maxpos`, `ap_sizing_shape`, `ap_ladder_shape`; and both partial-unique indexes `ux_ap_name` (case-insensitive name per account, live rows only) and `ux_ap_default` (one `is_default` per account).
- Trigger `trg_ap_ladder_sum` enforcing `SUM(pct) <= 100` over the `tp_ladder` JSONB array (an aggregation, so it cannot be a CHECK).
- Enum types required by the DDL: `sizing_mode`, `offset_unit`, `trade_group_status` (`draft`,`submitting`,`partially_open`,`open`,`closing`,`closed`,`failed`,`cancelled`).
- Alembic migration creating `trade_groups` (SS3.3.2) with indexes `ix_tg_open`, `ix_tg_user_time`, `ix_tg_rule`, `ix_tg_env_time`, and `trade_group_legs` (SS3.3.3) with `profile_snapshot jsonb NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE (trade_group_id, exchange_account_id)` and indexes `ix_tgl_group`, `ix_tgl_account`, `ix_tgl_open`, `ix_tgl_no_sl`.
- SQLAlchemy models and repository layer in `services/api/candleviewer/profiles/` and `candleviewer/oms/groups/`, with soft-delete (`deleted_at`) honoured in every read path.
- Pydantic domain models `AccountProfile`, `TradeGroup`, `TradeGroupLeg`, `TakeProfitLeg`, `TradeGroupAggregate` transcribed from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.1-SS9.2, with `Decimal` everywhere a value crosses into the OMS, journal or audit (invariant C3 of `24-internal-schemas.md`).
- Profile **versioning**: `version` integer on the domain model, bumped on every update; historical versions retained so `trade_group_legs.profile_snapshot` and journal attribution can point at the exact version used (US-PROF-001 scenario "Profile in use").
- Seed/bootstrap: creating an exchange account with no profile auto-creates a disabled default profile named "Default" so an account is never profile-less in the data model; it is flagged `trading_enabled = false` until the owner completes it.
- Downgrade path for every migration, and a migration test that runs `upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade` on a scratch database.

## Out of scope
REST routes (E28-T02); sizing arithmetic (E28-T03); risk-cap evaluation in the order path (E28-T04); group membership API and WS projection (E28-T05); any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given an empty Postgres 16 database with the R3 baseline schema applied
  When the E28 migrations run forward, then back, then forward again
  Then all three tables, all enums, all indexes and the ladder trigger exist and match the DDL in 21-database-schema.md byte for byte in shape

Scenario: The native-SL invariant is enforced by the database
  When an INSERT or UPDATE sets account_profiles.require_native_sl to false
  Then the statement is rejected by constraint ap_native_sl and no row is written

Scenario: Sizing shape is enforced by the database
  When a profile is written with sizing_mode 'risk_based' and size_fixed_qty set
  Then the statement is rejected by constraint ap_sizing_shape

Scenario: Exactly one default profile per account
  Given account A already has a profile with is_default true and deleted_at null
  When a second default profile is inserted for account A
  Then the unique index ux_ap_default rejects it

Scenario: TP ladder percentages cannot exceed 100
  When a profile is saved with tp_ladder [{"pct":60,"r":1},{"pct":60,"r":2}]
  Then trigger trg_ap_ladder_sum rejects the write with a message naming the 100% limit

Scenario: A soft-deleted profile frees its name
  Given profile "Scalp" on account A is soft-deleted
  When a new profile named "scalp" is created on account A
  Then it is accepted, because ux_ap_name is a partial index over deleted_at IS NULL

Scenario: Leg snapshot survives a profile edit
  Given a trade-group leg was created from profile version 3
  When the profile is edited to version 4
  Then the leg's profile_snapshot still contains version 3's values, unchanged
```

## Technical notes / design
Profile versioning is implemented as a monotonic `version` column plus an append-only `account_profile_revisions` projection written by the same transaction as the update (id, profile_id, version, payload jsonb, changed_by, changed_at). Revisions are what the journal and `trade_group_legs.profile_snapshot` reconcile against; the live row stays the fast read path. Snapshots are stored as a full frozen copy rather than a version pointer so a hard profile delete can never orphan a historical trade (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.1: "frozen copy - profiles change over time").

`allowed_symbols` and `blocked_symbols` are `text[]`; NULL/empty `allowed_symbols` means "all listed linear USDT perps" (US-PROF-003 scenario "Empty list means all"), and `blocked_symbols` is applied *after* the allow-list. Wildcard patterns (`*USDT`) are stored literally and expanded at evaluation time in E28-T04 against the instrument cache - never expanded at write time, so a newly listed symbol matching the pattern is covered automatically.

Money and quantity columns are `numeric(38,18)`; the ORM maps them to `Decimal` with no float round-trip anywhere. Percentages are `numeric(9,6)` and are stored as the user-visible percent (0..100) in Postgres while the Pydantic `AccountProfile` uses fractions 0..1 (`pct_equity`, `risk_pct_equity` documented as 0..1 in `24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2) - the mapping happens in exactly one adapter function, `to_domain()`/`to_row()`, and is unit-tested both directions.

Error codes surfaced to callers by the repository layer: `validation_failed` with a `constraint` detail naming the violated CHECK, `conflict` for unique-index violations, `native_stop_mandatory` for `ap_native_sl` specifically (the OpenAPI document names this code for `PUT .../profiles/{profileId}`).

## Test plan
Unit: constraint matrix - one test per CHECK, asserting the exact constraint name in the raised error; sizing-shape matrix over all four `sizing_mode` values x all four size columns; percent/fraction adapter round-trip; soft-delete visibility in every repository read.
Integration: migration up/down/up on a scratch Postgres 16 container; ladder trigger with 0, 1, 5 and over-100 entries; concurrent default-profile insert under two transactions asserting exactly one succeeds.
Property test: random valid `AccountProfile` instances round-trip domain -> row -> domain with `Decimal` equality.
Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/profiles/{risk_based,fixed_qty,pct_equity,fixed_notional}.json` reused by E28-T03 and E28-Q01.
Coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles`.

## Security notes
Asset A-08 (per-account profiles) and A-09 (trade-group configuration) from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SS4, both classified Confidential with integrity rating 3. Threat **Tampering (O3)**: a profile row whose caps are widened escalates position size on every subsequent order - mitigated here by the database-level CHECKs, which hold even if an application-layer bug lets a bad payload through, and by the append-only revision table that makes a silent edit impossible. Threat **F6**: a leg placed without a native SL because the profile lacked offsets - mitigated by `sl_offset_value > 0 NOT NULL` and `ap_native_sl`. No secret material is stored in these tables; `profile_snapshot` must never embed API-key fields, asserted by a serialisation test.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Profile reads sit on the order path and must be cache-friendly: the repository exposes `get_effective_profile(account_id, profile_id | None)` returning a frozen dataclass, backed by an in-process cache keyed by `(profile_id, version)` and invalidated by the update path. Target: cached read <=50 us, cold read <=2 ms. The whole dataset is at most a few dozen rows in v1 (6 accounts), so index choice matters for `trade_group_legs`, not for profiles.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_profile_rows_total{account}`, `cv_profile_version_bumps_total`, `cv_profile_cache_hit_ratio`.
Audit (written by E28-T02, schema reserved here): `profile.created`, `profile.updated`, `profile.deleted` with full before/after diff.
Logs: migration start/finish with the revision id at INFO; constraint violations logged at WARN with the constraint name, never with the payload.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27** (the `exchange_accounts` table these rows hang off, plus the account CASCADE semantics) and by **E28-X01** (the STRIDE model, whose findings may add a column or a constraint before the migration is frozen). `trade_group_legs` references `orders`, which **E29** owns; land the FK as nullable and add the constraint in E29's migration if E29's table has not merged yet - the ordering is recorded in the migration's docstring.

## Branch
`feat/e28-profile-schema` - two PRs: (1) enums + `account_profiles` + revisions + trigger, (2) `trade_groups` + `trade_group_legs` + domain models. Each <=400 LOC.

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#7-r3--trading-on-demo` - E28 scope line (26 pts, S15-S16), R3 exit criteria #2, #3, #4, quality gates SS7.4, key dates SS7.5

title: Implement profile CRUD routes with exchange-limit validation and audited step-up saves
body:
## Context
US-PROF-001 ("Define a per-account profile", Must) requires that a profile is "versioned, saved and shown on every ticket targeting that account", that invalid combinations are blocked "with a field-level explanation", and that editing a profile with open positions "creates a new version; existing positions keep their originating version for journal attribution". Its NFR is explicit: "profile is server-enforced on every order path, not just the UI".

The REST surface is already frozen in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET`/`POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles` and `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles/{profileId}`. The spec also states the two rules this Task must implement literally: `require_native_stop` "cannot be set to `false` ... Attempting `false` returns `validation_failed` / `native_stop_mandatory`", and `DELETE` is "refused with `conflict` when the profile is the account's active profile or is referenced by an armed rule".

SCR-131 (Admin: profile editor) adds the validation rules that make a profile safe on a real exchange: "leverage <= the exchange maximum for every allowed symbol (`SOLUSDT allows at most 20x - your 25x would be rejected`); daily loss between -0.1% and -50%; max position >= min lot; sizing rule must produce >= min lot at the current equity, otherwise a warning with a worked example". Its performance line requires the save round-trip, including revalidation against the exchange's current limits, to target <=2 s.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Router `services/api/candleviewer/profiles/routes.py` implementing `listAccountProfiles`, `createAccountProfile`, `getAccountProfile`, `updateAccountProfile`, `deleteAccountProfile` exactly per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, with the documented `x-rbac` (`accounts:read` / `accounts:write`, scope `granted_accounts`), `Idempotency-Key` handling (recommended on POST, optional on PUT) and `If-Match` optimistic concurrency returning `412 PreconditionFailed`.
- `ProfileValidator` service implementing the SCR-131 rule set against the instrument cache from **E08**: leverage <= `min(leverageFilter.maxLeverage)` over every symbol in the effective allowed set; `max_position_notional_usd` >= `min_notional`; `size_fixed_qty` >= `lotSizeFilter.minOrderQty` and a multiple of `qtyStep`; SL/TP offsets in ticks must be a positive multiple of `tickSize` when `unit = ticks`; `max_daily_loss` between 0.1% and 50% of equity when expressed as a percent.
- Cross-field shape validation with **field-level** error payloads: `{"code":"validation_failed","errors":[{"field":"risk_pct_equity","message":"Risk-based sizing needs a risk percentage."}]}` - US-PROF-001 scenario "Invalid combination" requires the explanation to be attached to the field, not the form.
- Risk-based sizing precondition: when `sizing_mode = risk_based`, either an SL offset resolving to a distance (`ticks`/`percent`/`atr`) must be present, or the request is rejected - `r_multiple` is invalid for the stop itself and "raises a validation error at profile save time" (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.3.1).
- Versioning and revision write: every successful `PUT` bumps `version`, writes an `account_profile_revisions` row and returns the new version in the `ETag`.
- **Step-up re-authentication** on create, update and delete per SR-025 of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` ("changing risk caps or per-account profiles" is on the step-up list); a request without a valid step-up token (password + TOTP, 5-minute validity) returns `403 step_up_required`.
- Audit events `profile.created`, `profile.updated`, `profile.deleted`, `profile.bound`, `profile.unbound` with a full before/after diff, emitted through the audit chain and never skippable (SCR-130: "audited with before/after, because a profile directly determines order size and leverage").
- Delete guard: `409 conflict` when the profile is `is_default`, is the account's active profile, or is referenced by an armed rule (`rules` scope `account`), with a message naming the blocker.
- Profile-change propagation: publish a `profiles` domain event onto the internal bus so open tickets refresh within the 2 s budget stated by SCR-130 ("Changes propagate to open tickets within 2 s over the private channel so a stale profile is never used for sizing").
- OpenAPI conformance test wiring so any drift between code and `22-api-openapi.yaml` fails CI.

## Out of scope
Trade-group routes (E28-T05); sizing arithmetic (E28-T03); order-path enforcement (E28-T04); the editor UI (E28-S01); templates UI (E28-S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create a risk-based profile
  Given account sub_001 exists with a verified key
  When the owner POSTs a profile with sizing mode risk_based, risk 0.5%, an ATR stop of 1.5x period 14, leverage 10 and allowed symbols BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT, with a valid step-up token
  Then 201 is returned with version 1, an ETag, and an audit row profile.created containing the full payload

Scenario: Risk-based without a stop is refused at save time
  When a profile is saved with sizing mode risk_based and no SL offset, or with an SL offset unit of r_multiple
  Then 422 validation_failed is returned with a field-level error on the stop definition, and no row is written

Scenario: Native stop cannot be disabled
  When any request sets require_native_stop to false
  Then 422 validation_failed with code native_stop_mandatory is returned, and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Leverage above the exchange maximum for an allowed symbol
  Given SOLUSDT is on the allowed list and Bybit caps it at 20x
  When the profile is saved with leverage 25
  Then 422 is returned naming SOLUSDT and its 20x maximum

Scenario: Concurrent edit loses safely
  Given two editors loaded profile version 3
  When the second one PUTs with If-Match for version 3 after the first has saved version 4
  Then 412 precondition_failed is returned and the second editor is told to reload

Scenario: Editing with open positions creates a new version
  Given open positions reference profile version 3
  When the profile is updated
  Then version 4 is stored, version 3 remains readable through the revisions projection, and the open positions still attribute to version 3

Scenario: Step-up is mandatory
  When an owner with a valid session but no step-up token updates a risk cap
  Then 403 step_up_required is returned, no row is written, and the refusal is audited

Scenario: A manager cannot touch an account they were not granted
  When a manager PUTs a profile on an account outside their grants
  Then 403 is returned, no state changes, and an audit row records the denied attempt

Scenario: Delete is refused while in use
  Given the profile is the account's default and an armed rule references it
  When DELETE is called
  Then 409 conflict is returned naming both blockers
```

## Technical notes / design
The validator runs in two passes. Pass 1 is pure shape validation from the Pydantic model (fast, no I/O) and produces field-level errors. Pass 2 is exchange-limit validation against the cached `instruments-info` snapshot for the account's environment; if the cache is older than 15 minutes the route refreshes it first (`instruments-info` has a 10 req/s ceiling per SR-044b, so the refresh is coalesced across concurrent saves by a single-flight lock). Pass 2 failures name the offending symbol and the exact limit, which is what SCR-131's copy requires.

When `allowed_symbols` is empty, pass 2 validates leverage against the *most restrictive* leverage cap in the whole listed USDT-perp universe, and the response includes a `warnings` array (`"allows all symbols - consider restricting"`) that SCR-130 renders as the `(!)` row marker. Warnings never block a save.

`If-Match` carries the opaque ETag `W/"<profile_id>:<version>"`. The update is executed as `UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND version = :version RETURNING *`; zero rows means 412.

Idempotency: `Idempotency-Key` is stored with the request-hash and the response for 24 h; a replay with the same key and the same body returns the stored response, a replay with a different body returns `409 idempotency_key_reuse`.

Error codes: `validation_failed`, `native_stop_mandatory`, `conflict`, `idempotency_key_reuse`, `precondition_failed`, `step_up_required`, `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `instrument_cache_unavailable` (503, with `Retry-After`).

## Test plan

title: Build the server-side leg sizer: sizing rules, stop resolution and lot/notional rounding
body:
## Context
US-PROF-002 ("Sizing rules", Must) is the arithmetic heart of this epic: percent-of-equity, fixed-notional, fixed-quantity and risk-based sizing, "so that size follows a policy instead of a guess". Its NFR is a security requirement as much as a correctness one: "all rounding uses instrument tick/lot filters; computation is server-verified on submit so a tampered client cannot oversize."

The algorithm is fully specified as pseudo-code in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.3 (`size_leg`) with stop resolution in SS9.3.1. This Task implements it as module **M13**'s `Sizer` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md`: "Applies per-account profile sizing rule; rounds to lot size; rejects if below min notional"; interface `size(account, cmd) -> Decimal`). It is consumed by the preview endpoint (E28-T05), the order ticket (E30), the fan-out engine (E34) and the rule engine (E35) - all of which must produce identical numbers, so this is the single implementation and no caller is permitted to re-derive size.

The story's Gherkin fixes the worked examples that become golden tests: equity 10 000 USDT, risk 0.5%, stop distance 120 USDT on BTCUSDT -> quantity computed, rounded **down** to the lot size, shown with implied risk in USDT and in R; 5% of equity at 10x -> notional, quantity and resulting initial margin; and a computed quantity below the minimum order quantity blocks submission, explains the minimum and offers it as a one-click choice.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `candleviewer/profiles/sizer.py` implementing `size_leg(intent, profile, wallet, instrument, metrics) -> LegSizing` per `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.3, in the exact documented order: profile enabled/trading-enabled check -> allowed-symbol check -> denied-symbol check -> stop resolution -> sizing-mode branch -> risk-based adjustment -> `clamp_to_caps` -> min-lot/min-notional feasibility -> available-margin feasibility.
- Four sizing modes with the documented formulae: `fixed_qty` -> `profile.fixed_qty`; `fixed_notional` -> `fixed_notional / ref`; `pct_equity` -> `(equity * pct_equity * leverage) / ref`; `risk_based` -> `risk_amt / stop_distance` where `risk_amt` is `risk_fixed_amount` when set, otherwise `equity * risk_pct_equity`.
- `resolve_stop` per SS9.3.1: `ticks` -> `ref +/- value * tick_size`; `percent` -> `ref * (1 -/+ value)`; `atr` -> `ref -/+ atr(period) * multiple`; `r_multiple` rejected for the stop itself; sign follows side (long -> stop below); the resolved stop is rounded **conservatively** (further from entry, never closer) so realised risk never exceeds the budget; when ATR is unavailable during warm-up, fall back to `fallback_sl_offset_pct` (default 2%) and set `stop_fallback = True` on the leg.
- `clamp_to_caps(qty, profile, wallet, ref, instrument)` applying `max_position_notional`, `max_position_pct_equity`, `max_leverage_cap` and the remaining headroom of `max_daily_loss` - clamping down only, never up.
- Rounding: quantity floored to `lotSizeFilter.qtyStep` (`qty_rounding = "floor"`), prices snapped to `priceFilter.tickSize`, all with `Decimal` and an explicit `ROUND_DOWN`/`ROUND_FLOOR` quantisation - no float arithmetic anywhere on this path (invariant C3).
- Outcome typing: a **skip** (`symbol_not_allowed`, `below_min_notional`, `profile_disabled`) is distinct from a **failure** (`INSUFFICIENT_MARGIN`, cap breach) - `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.6 requires these never be conflated, because the UI renders skips grey and failures red.
- Returned explanation object: computed qty, notional, implied risk in USDT **and in R**, resulting initial margin, the resolved stop, the rounding delta, and the ordered list of rules that fired - this is what the ticket and the preview render, so it is part of the contract, not a debug aid.
- Golden-vector fixture `tests/golden/sizing/e28_vectors.json` with at least 40 cases covering all four modes x {long, short} x {tick, percent, ATR stops} x {inside caps, clamped, below min lot, insufficient margin}, generated once and reviewed, then frozen.
- Benchmark harness asserting the per-leg budget.

## Out of scope
Order submission and the native-SL attach (E29/E32); the rate-limit governor and parallel dispatch (E34); the preview REST endpoint (E28-T05); UI (E28-S01, E28-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Risk-based sizing matches the story's worked example
  Given equity 10000 USDT, risk 0.5% and a stop distance of 120 USDT on BTCUSDT
  When the leg is sized
  Then quantity is 0.416 rounded down to the 0.001 lot step, and the result reports implied risk in USDT and in R

Scenario: Percent-of-equity reports margin
  Given the rule is 5% of equity at 10x with equity 10000 and a reference price of 64000
  Then the result reports notional 5000, quantity floored to the lot step, and the resulting initial margin 500

Scenario: Below the minimum lot is a skip, not a crash
  Given the computed quantity is 0.0004 BTC and the minimum order quantity is 0.001
  Then the outcome is a skip with reason below_min_notional, the minimum is reported, and no exception is raised

Scenario: Rounding never increases risk
  Given any risk-based case
  When quantity is rounded to the lot step
  Then the rounding direction is down and the recomputed implied risk is less than or equal to the budgeted risk

Scenario: Conservative stop rounding
  Given a stop that falls between two ticks
  Then the stored stop is the tick further from entry, never the nearer one

Scenario: ATR warm-up fallback
  Given the ATR(14) series has fewer than 14 closed bars
  Then the stop falls back to fallback_sl_offset_pct, the leg is flagged stop_fallback true, and sizing still succeeds

Scenario: Symbol not allowed is a skip with a named reason
  Given DOGEUSDT is absent from the profile's allowed list
  Then the outcome is skip with reason symbol_not_allowed

Scenario: Caps clamp downward only
  Given the computed notional exceeds max_position_notional
  Then the quantity is reduced to the cap and the explanation names the cap that bound it, and quantity is never raised by a clamp

Scenario: Insufficient margin is a failure, not a skip
  Given the sized notional needs more than 98% of available margin at the profile's leverage
  Then the outcome is a failure with code INSUFFICIENT_MARGIN

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the frozen golden vector file
  When the sizer runs over every vector
  Then every output matches the recorded value exactly, to the last decimal place
```

## Technical notes / design
Everything is `Decimal`. The reference price `ref` is the order's limit price for limit orders and the current mark price for market orders; the caller passes it in, the sizer never fetches it, which keeps the function pure and therefore golden-testable. `wallet` is a frozen snapshot (equity, available margin) and `instrument` a frozen snapshot (tick size, qty step, min order qty, min notional, max leverage) - both taken once per fan-out so all legs of one group size against a consistent view.

R is defined as the risk budget of the leg: `implied_R_value = stop_distance * qty`. Reporting risk "in R" means the ticket shows `1R = <implied_R_value> USDT`, which is what US-PROF-002's first scenario asks for.

The margin feasibility check uses the documented 98% factor: `qty * ref > available_margin * leverage * 0.98` -> failure. The 2% head-room absorbs fee and funding drift between preview and submit.

The function returns `LegSizing` with a discriminated outcome (`ok` | `skip` | `fail`), never raising for business outcomes; exceptions are reserved for programming errors. This matters because the fan-out engine (E34) iterates legs and must not lose the rest of a group to one bad account.

Config keys: `profiles.sizer.margin_headroom` (default `0.98`), `profiles.sizer.atr_default_period` (14), `profiles.sizer.fallback_sl_offset_pct` (0.02), `profiles.sizer.max_legs_per_group` (cap 20, matching the Business-KYC sub-account ceiling).

## Test plan
Unit: the 40+ golden vectors; one test per branch of `size_leg`; `resolve_stop` per unit x side x rounding direction; `clamp_to_caps` per cap; skip-vs-failure classification table.
Property tests (Hypothesis): for random valid inputs, (a) realised risk <= budgeted risk, (b) quantity is always a non-negative multiple of `qtyStep`, (c) clamping is monotonic and never increases quantity, (d) no float ever appears in the output (asserted by type inspection).
Integration: sizer driven from a real profile row and a recorded wallet/instrument fixture.
Perf: benchmark - 5 legs sized in <=5 ms total, single leg p95 <=1 ms, run in CI with a regression threshold.
Coverage >=90% - this module is on the roadmap's >=90% list.

## Security notes
This module *is* control **SR-052** ("Order sizing, leverage, SL/TP offsets and risk caps MUST be computed and enforced server-side from the per-account profile. Client-provided values are hints and MUST be clamped or rejected, never trusted") and **SR-053**. Threat O3 (Tampering - quantity/price/leverage manipulated beyond profile caps, rated High) is closed here: the client's proposed quantity is accepted only as an upper-bound hint and is re-derived server-side; a hint larger than the computed size is clamped and the clamp is recorded. Threat F2 (one account getting another's sizing) is prevented by taking the profile from the leg's own `profile_snapshot`, never from the request. An abuse-case test in E28-X03 submits a crafted oversized hint and asserts the clamp plus the audit row.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend. The explanation object's wording feeds screen-reader text in the ticket, so its strings are reviewed with design (E28-D06) and contain units, never bare numbers.

## Performance notes
Budget: single-leg sizing p95 <=1 ms, 5-leg group <=5 ms of the fan-out's <=50 ms + <=10 ms/account backend overhead (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` SS5.2 budget #4 fan-out sub-clause). ATR values come from the indicator cache; a cache miss must not block - it takes the documented fallback path instead.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_sizer_duration_seconds` histogram, `cv_sizer_outcomes_total{outcome,reason}`, `cv_sizer_clamped_total{cap}`, `cv_sizer_stop_fallback_total`.
Logs: one structured DEBUG line per leg with inputs and outputs (no secrets) behind a sampling flag; WARN on `stop_fallback`.
Audit: the sizing explanation is embedded in the leg's `profile_snapshot` sibling field so any order can be re-derived after the fact.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.

- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.

## Dependencies

Consumes the instrument cache and mark prices from **E08**, wallet snapshots from **E27**, and ATR from the indicator framework in **E13**. Consumed by **E28-T05**, **E30**, **E34** and **E35** - the interface is therefore frozen after review and any change is a contract change.

title: Enforce allowed symbols and risk caps inside the order path with audited refusals
body:
## Context
US-PROF-003 ("Allowed-symbol restriction", Must) and US-PROF-004 ("Risk caps enforced server-side", Must) exist because the UI is not a security boundary. US-PROF-004's wording is unambiguous: "I want max position size, max daily loss and max concurrent positions enforced in the backend, so that limits survive a broken or hostile client", with the NFR "evaluated inside the order path before any exchange call; evaluation adds <=5 ms p95". US-PROF-003 adds "When a crafted request submits a DOGEUSDT order for account B / Then the server rejects with 403 and audits the attempt".

`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3.5 places this check in the OMS pipeline between validation and fan-out (`API->>RISK: check(intent, account, profile)` in `24-internal-schemas.md` SS8). This Task delivers that `RiskGuard` for the profile-owned caps; the global/daily lockout state machine and the kill-switch belong to **E39** and this guard calls into it rather than duplicating it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `candleviewer/profiles/guard.py` exposing `check(intent, account_id, profile) -> GuardVerdict`, called by the OMS (**E29**) before any exchange call, by the rule engine (**E35**) before any rule action, and by the fan-out planner (**E34**) per leg.
- Symbol gate: effective allow-list = `allowed_symbols` (empty/NULL = all listed linear USDT perps) minus `blocked_symbols`, with wildcard expansion (`*USDT`) evaluated against the live instrument cache at check time, so a newly listed symbol matching a pattern is covered without a profile edit (US-PROF-003 NFR).
- Cap gates, each with its own verdict code and human message:
  - `max_position_notional_usd` / `max_position_pct_equity` - evaluated against the *resulting* position after this order, producing the story's message shape "would exceed max position 0.5 BTC (current 0.4)".
  - `max_open_positions` - counts distinct open symbols; when at the cap, new-symbol entries are refused **while reduce-only orders remain allowed** (US-PROF-004 scenario 2).
  - `max_concurrent_orders` and `max_orders_per_minute` - a per-account sliding-window counter; over budget returns a retry-after rather than a hard failure.
  - `max_daily_loss` / `max_daily_loss_pct` - when realised+unrealised loss reaches the cap, the guard refuses new entries and delegates lockout to **E39** (US-PROF-004 scenario 3 references US-RULE-012).
  - `max_leverage_cap` - refuses an order whose effective leverage exceeds the profile cap.
- Reduce-only exemption matrix, written once and unit-tested: which gates a reduce-only or position-closing order bypasses (open-position count, symbol allow-list for an *existing* position) and which it never bypasses (kill-switch, account disabled).
- HTTP mapping: profile refusals surface as `403` with `code = profile_forbidden` for the symbol gate (US-PROF-003 explicitly asks for 403) and `422 risk_limit_breached` for cap breaches, matching the WS example in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (`"code":"risk_limit_breached","message":"max_daily_loss_usd 1500 already realised (-1522.40)"`).
- Audit on every refusal: `order.refused_by_profile` with the account, symbol, the gate that fired, the observed value and the cap - so a crafted request leaves a trail (US-PROF-003 scenario 2).
- Daily-loss accounting: realised PnL from `executions` plus unrealised from the position snapshot, rolled over at 00:00 UTC, with the rollover boundary configurable per deployment and covered by a test at the boundary.
- Hot-path caching: the guard reads the E28-T01 profile cache and a per-account counters structure in memory, rebuilt from Postgres on start-up and on reconnect.

## Out of scope
The lockout state machine, its 2FA-gated reset and the kill-switch (**E39**); the native-SL invariant enforcement (**E32**); rate-limit token buckets against Bybit's per-UID budgets (**E34** - this ticket owns only the profile's own `max_orders_per_minute`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Symbol not permitted is refused and audited
  Given DOGEUSDT is not on account B's allowed list
  When a crafted API request submits a DOGEUSDT order for account B
  Then the response is 403 profile_forbidden, no exchange call is made, and an audit row names the account, the symbol and the gate

Scenario: Empty allow-list permits every listed USDT perp
  Given account C's allowed_symbols is empty
  When an order for any listed linear USDT perpetual is checked
  Then the symbol gate passes

Scenario: Wildcards follow new listings
  Given the allow-list contains *USDT and a new symbol NEWUSDT is listed by Bybit
  When an order for NEWUSDT is checked without any profile edit
  Then the symbol gate passes

Scenario: Position-size cap
  Given account C caps position size at 0.5 BTC and holds 0.4 BTC
  When an order for 0.2 BTC is submitted
  Then it is rejected with "would exceed max position 0.5 BTC (current 0.4)"

Scenario: Concurrent-position cap still allows reduce-only
  Given the cap is 3 and 3 positions are open
  When an order would open a fourth symbol
  Then it is rejected; and when a reduce-only order on an existing position is submitted, it is allowed

Scenario: Daily-loss cap refuses entries and hands over to lockout
  Given realised plus unrealised loss reaches the profile's daily cap
  When a new entry is submitted
  Then it is refused with risk_limit_breached, the lockout service is notified once, and the refusal is audited

Scenario: Daily loss rolls over at 00:00 UTC
  Given the cap was breached at 23:59 UTC
  When the clock passes 00:00 UTC
  Then the day's accumulator resets and entries are permitted again unless a lockout from E39 still stands

Scenario: The guard cannot be bypassed
  Given a request that supplies its own "risk_checked" hint
  Then the hint is ignored and the guard runs regardless

Scenario: Evaluation stays inside its budget
  Given a warm cache
  When 1000 checks run
  Then p95 evaluation time is at or below 5 ms
```

## Technical notes / design
The guard is a pure function over (intent, profile snapshot, position snapshot, counters, instrument) and is therefore table-testable. Ordering of the gates is fixed and documented, cheapest and most-categorical first: account enabled -> kill-switch (E39) -> symbol gate -> leverage cap -> open-position count -> position notional -> order-rate -> daily loss. The first refusal short-circuits, so the message the user sees is the most fundamental reason, not an arbitrary one.

Counters live in a per-account `AccountRiskState` kept in memory and updated from the OMS execution stream; on start-up and on every WS reconnect it is rebuilt from Postgres (`orders`, `executions`, `positions`) so a restart cannot reopen a breached cap. Rebuild completeness is asserted by a chaos test in E28-Q03.

`max_orders_per_minute` uses a 60-second sliding window of timestamps per account, not a fixed bucket, so a burst across a bucket boundary cannot double the allowance.

Error codes: `profile_forbidden`, `risk_limit_breached`, `account_locked_out`, `account_disabled`, `rate_budget_exhausted` (with `retry_after_ms`).

## Test plan
Unit: gate-order table; one test per gate for pass, boundary (exactly at the cap) and breach; reduce-only exemption matrix; wildcard expansion including a pattern that matches nothing; UTC rollover at the boundary second.
Integration: guard wired into the OMS submit path with a fake exchange asserting **zero** exchange calls on refusal; counter rebuild after a simulated process restart mid-day.
Security/abuse: crafted requests - symbol not allowed, oversized quantity hint, spoofed account id, client-supplied "already checked" flag - each asserting refusal, no state change and an audit row (feeds E28-X03).
Perf: 1000-iteration benchmark asserting p95 <=5 ms with a warm cache; a cold-cache path measured separately and documented.
Chaos: guard behaviour when the position snapshot is stale or unavailable - it must fail **closed** (refuse) rather than open.
Coverage >=90%.

## Security notes
Implements **SR-052**, **SR-053** and **SR-054**, and is the enforcement point that makes US-PROF-003 and US-PROF-004 true against a hostile client. Threats closed: O3 (Tampering with size/leverage), F2 (per-account profile ignored so one account gets another's sizing - the guard always reads the leg's own profile snapshot). Fail-closed behaviour is a stated requirement: if the guard cannot evaluate a cap because its inputs are unavailable, it refuses the order and raises an alert rather than letting it through. Every refusal is audited (SR-064); refusal audit rows are the evidence trail for the abuse-case review in E28-X03. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend. Refusal messages are user-visible strings and must be plain language with units and the observed value, since screen readers will read them verbatim in `role="alert"` regions in E30's ticket.

## Performance notes
Budget: <=5 ms p95 added to the order path (US-PROF-004 NFR), inside the overall order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms hard gate (budget #4). Cache reads only on the hot path; any I/O in the guard is a defect and is asserted against by a test that fails if the database session is touched during `check()`.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_risk_guard_seconds` histogram, `cv_risk_guard_refusals_total{gate}`, `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total`, `cv_account_daily_loss_usd{account}` gauge, `cv_account_open_positions{account}` gauge.
Alerts: `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total` > 0 in 5 minutes pages the owner; a cap breach raises a `warning` notification.
Audit: `order.refused_by_profile{gate, observed, limit}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T03** (the sizer whose output the caps clamp and check) and **E29** (the OMS submit pipeline this guard plugs into, and the execution stream that feeds the counters). Calls into **E39** for lockout transitions and the kill-switch; E39 owns that state, this ticket only notifies and reads it. Consumes positions from **E29** and instruments from **E08**.

## Branch

title: Spike: per-trade override semantics and profile-change propagation to open tickets
body:
## Context
US-PROF-008 ("Per-trade profile overrides", Should) is the one part of this epic the plan marks as unresolved: its Refs line points at `OD "still open" SSper-account profile detail`, meaning the owner recorded the *shape* of overrides but not the exact rule set. The story fixes three invariants - an override "never widens a hard risk cap", it "resets to the profile default for the next ticket" after submit or cancel, and every override is "audited and journal-tagged" - but leaves open which fields are overridable at all, and how an override interacts with a profile edited mid-ticket.

The second open question is propagation. SCR-130 states "Changes propagate to open tickets within 2 s over the private channel so a stale profile is never used for sizing", but the WS topic catalogue in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` has no `profiles` topic - private topics are flat and enumerated (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`, `rules`, `alerts`, `recorder`, `system`). Either propagation rides an existing topic or the protocol needs an addition, and the protocol is frozen for R3 unless a decision says otherwise. This must be settled before E28-T02 finishes and before E28-S05 is designed.

This is a 2-day timebox, not production code.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Decision table: for each field of `AccountProfile` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2), whether it is (a) overridable freely, (b) overridable downward only, or (c) never overridable. Starting position from the plan: leverage is capped (SCR-061 shows "capped by profile" on the control), size is overridable within the risk cap, allowed symbols are never overridable, `require_native_sl` is never overridable.
- Decision on override lifetime: per-ticket only (reset on submit or cancel) versus per-session, with the evidence for the choice.
- Decision on propagation transport: reuse of an existing private topic versus a `system` sub-event versus a REST re-fetch triggered by an existing event, measured against the 2 s budget and against the rule that the WS topic list is frozen for R3.
- Decision on mid-ticket profile edits: what happens to an open ticket whose profile changed underneath it (silent re-price, explicit "profile changed - review" state, or block).
- A throwaway prototype measuring end-to-end propagation latency from `PUT /profiles/{id}` to a ticket re-render over the chosen transport, on the R3 staging topology over Tailscale.
- **ADR-0016 "Per-trade profile overrides and profile propagation"** written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, following the ADR template, recording the decision even if it is "defer" (per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS5.2).
- Follow-up tickets filed against whichever path is chosen, with the findings linked.

## Out of scope
Implementing the chosen design (E28-T02 for propagation, E28-S05 for overrides); any change to the OMS or to E34's fan-out.

## Acceptance criteria
- The override decision table covers every field of `AccountProfile` with no field left unclassified, and is signed off by the Owner and the Architect.
- Propagation latency is measured, with a number recorded for the chosen transport, and it is at or below the 2 s budget stated in SCR-130 - or the transport is rejected and an alternative is measured.
- The mid-ticket-edit behaviour is decided and expressed as Gherkin that E28-S05 and E30 can consume directly.
- ADR-0016 is merged with status `decided` (or `deferred` with the missing input named and an owner assigned).
- Follow-up tickets exist and are linked; the prototype branch is either promoted through a normal Task or explicitly marked throwaway and left unmerged.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if the spike surfaced or retired a risk.

## Technical notes / design
Timebox: 2 days, agreed with the Architect. Decision rule agreed up front: if reusing an existing private topic cannot meet the 2 s budget without conflation loss, the fallback is an event-triggered REST re-fetch (`GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`) rather than adding a topic, because the R3 protocol freeze (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS5 item 4) outranks transport elegance.

The safety floor is fixed before the spike starts and is not up for negotiation: no override may widen `max_position_notional`, `max_daily_loss`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage_cap`, the allowed-symbol set, or `require_native_sl`. The spike decides only the permitted *narrowing* and the UX of expressing it.

## Test plan
Not a production-code ticket. The prototype carries a latency measurement script committed under `spikes/e28-override-propagation/` with its raw results, so the number can be reproduced.

## Security notes
The override surface is a privilege-escalation vector: an override that widens a cap defeats SR-052, SR-053 and SR-054 in one step. The decision table is therefore reviewed by the Security engineer as part of E28-X01's threat model, and the "downward only" property becomes an automated test in E28-S05 rather than a convention.

## Accessibility notes
The chosen override UX must be expressible without colour alone and must announce the "capped by profile" disabled reason, per SCR-061. The spike records the constraint for the designer; it does not design the control.

## Performance notes
Propagation budget 2 s end to end (SCR-130). Preview recomputation triggered by a propagation event must stay inside SCR-061's <=300 ms preview budget.

## Observability
Whichever transport wins, the follow-up ticket must add `cv_profile_propagation_seconds` so the 2 s budget is observable in production rather than only at spike time.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both questions answered with recorded evidence (decision table, measured latency numbers, prototype branch link).
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` with a status.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed and linked, with findings attached so implementers do not re-derive them.
- [ ] Prototype code promoted or explicitly marked throwaway; branch left unmerged if throwaway.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review and at the Design Review that precedes E28-D03.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated.
- [ ] Explicitly recorded on the ticket that this spike is not expected to produce production-shippable code.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T01** (the profile model the decision table is written against). Its output blocks **E28-S05** (overrides) and informs **E28-T02** (propagation) and **E30** (the ticket that renders overrides).

## Branch

title: Implement trade-group definition, preview endpoint and the trade_groups WS projection
body:
## Context
US-PROF-005 ("Create a trade group", Must) requires a named set of accounts that appears "in the ticket's target selector with a member count", refuses to mix demo and live accounts, and shows "2 of 3 ready" when a member's key fails its self-check - with the NFR "group membership is server-side truth; group edits audited".

The preview half comes from US-PROF-006 and from the roadmap's E28 scope line, which names "profile simulation preview ('this ticket would place X on A, Y on B')" as an E28 deliverable. `POST /trade-groups/preview` is already specified in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: it "runs the full fan-out pipeline (24-internal-schemas.md section 9.3 sizing, 9.4 fan-out) **without submitting anything**, returning exactly what each leg would send. Legs that would be rejected ... are returned with their reason ... Never mutates state and is therefore safe to call on every keystroke; it is rate-limited rather than idempotency-keyed."

The division of labour with **E34** is deliberate and must be respected: E28 owns the group *definition*, the *preview* and the *read* projection; E34 owns actual submission, the per-UID rate-limit governor and partial-failure remediation. This Task must therefore not place a single order.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Routes per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET /trade-groups` (`listTradeGroups`, cursor-paged, filterable by symbol, status, from/to; `orders:read`, scope `granted_accounts`), `POST /trade-groups` (definition/creation), `GET /trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}` ("with all legs and resolved parameters"), and `POST /trade-groups/preview` (`previewTradeGroup`, `orders:read`, returns `TradeGroupPreview`).
- Group definition model and persistence on `trade_groups` plus membership with per-account enable/disable, name uniqueness, and the `>=1 account` rule (SCR-062: "a group needs >=1 account; accounts must share at least one allowed symbol ... group names unique").
- **Mixed-environment guard**: a group may not contain both demo and live accounts; the create/amend request is refused with a message naming the offending accounts (US-PROF-005 scenario 2). Enforced server-side and also as a database-level check on `trade_groups.env` versus each member's `exchange_accounts.env`.
- **Empty symbol intersection warning**: when members' effective allowed-symbol sets have no symbol in common, saving is refused with SCR-062's message "These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything."
- Readiness computation: per-member readiness from the account health and key self-check state delivered by **E27** (`ready`, `not ready: key self-check failed`, `not ready: account disabled`, `not ready: locked out`), aggregated as the "N of M ready" string the UI renders.
- Preview pipeline: for each member account, load the effective profile, the wallet snapshot and the instrument snapshot once, call the **E28-T03** sizer, apply the **E28-T04** guard, and return per-leg `{account, profile_name, qty, leverage, stop_loss, take_profits, notional, implied_risk, status: ready|warn|skipped|blocked, reason}` plus the aggregate totals SCR-061 shows ("total 0.430 BTC - 27,525 USDT - est. fee 1.9"), with the maker/taker fee taken from the cached `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate`.
- Preview safety: strictly read-only - asserted by a test that runs a preview inside a transaction and fails if any write occurs - and rate-limited per user (token bucket, default 20 req/s) rather than idempotency-keyed, exactly as the spec says.
- WS projection for the `trade_groups` topic per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS15.5: `TradeGroupUpdate` frames with subscription options `exchange_account_ids` and `status`, a 100 ms throttle, `orders:read` plus granted-account intersection, and the causal-order guarantee S5 (`executions` -> `orders` -> `positions` -> `trade_groups`). Frame shape follows the documented example including `totals` and per-leg `status`/`error`.
- Audit events `tradegroup.created|updated|deleted|granted` and `tradegroup.preview`.

## Out of scope
Submitting a group (`POST /trade-groups` *execution* semantics), amend and cancel behaviour, the rate-limit governor, partial-failure remediation and unwind - all **E34**. Native-SL attach - **E32**. UI - E28-S03, E28-S04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create a group
  Given accounts A, B and C all exist in the demo environment
  When the owner creates a group named "Core3" containing all three
  Then the group is stored, appears in GET /trade-groups with a member count of 3, and an audit row tradegroup.created is written

Scenario: Mixed environments refused
  When a group is saved containing one demo account and one live account
  Then the request is refused with a message naming both accounts and stating that a trade group cannot mix Demo and Live

Scenario: Empty symbol intersection refused
  Given account A allows only BTCUSDT and account B allows only ETHUSDT
  When they are saved as one group
  Then the request is refused with "These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything."

Scenario: Readiness reflects key health
  Given account B's key self-check is failing
  When the group is read
  Then the group reports "2 of 3 ready" and account B carries a textual reason

Scenario: Preview resolves each leg by its own profile
  Given Main uses risk 0.5% of equity, sub_001 uses fixed 0.1 BTC and sub_002 uses risk 0.5% of equity
  When a preview is requested for a BTCUSDT buy with a stop
  Then three legs are returned with per-account quantity, leverage and stop, and the aggregate totals sum the legs

Scenario: Preview reports skips with reasons rather than failing
  Given sub_003 does not allow the symbol and sub_004 would size below the minimum lot
  When a preview is requested
  Then sub_003 is returned as skipped with symbol_not_allowed and sub_004 as skipped with below_min_notional, and the other legs are unaffected

Scenario: Preview never writes
  When a preview is called one hundred times
  Then no row is created or modified in trade_groups, trade_group_legs or orders, and no exchange call is made

Scenario: Preview is rate-limited, not idempotency-keyed
  When previews exceed the configured per-user rate
  Then 429 is returned with Retry-After, and no Idempotency-Key is ever required

Scenario: WS scoping is server-derived
  Given a manager granted only account A subscribes to trade_groups with exchange_account_ids for A, B and C
  Then only frames for A are delivered, the subscription is accepted without error, and the denied ids are not echoed back

Scenario: Preview latency
  Given five member accounts with warm caches
  When a preview is requested
  Then the p95 response time is at or below 300 ms
```

## Technical notes / design
Preview is implemented as `plan_group(intent, group) -> TradeGroupPreview`, the same planner E34 will call before dispatch - E34 adds submission and the governor around it rather than reimplementing it. Sharing the planner is what makes SCR-061's promise honest: what the preview shows is literally what would be sent.

Snapshots (wallet, instrument, positions) are taken **once per preview** and passed to every leg, so all legs size against one consistent view; a leg is never allowed to fetch its own price.

The `trade_groups` WS projection is a read model built from `trade_groups` + `trade_group_legs`, updated by domain events and conflated at 100 ms. Because the topic is flat and scoped by subscription options (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`: private topics "are **scoped by subscription options** ... which the server intersects with the caller's grants"), the server intersects requested `exchange_account_ids` with the caller's grants and silently narrows - it never errors on an over-broad request, and never reveals which ids were removed.

Error codes: `validation_failed` (empty membership, duplicate name, no common symbol), `env_mismatch`, `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `rate_limited` (429 with `Retry-After`).

Config keys: `tradegroups.preview.rate_per_user_per_second` (20), `tradegroups.max_members` (20 - the Business-KYC sub-account ceiling), `tradegroups.readiness_refresh_seconds` (30, matching US-PROF-007's reconciliation cadence).

## Test plan
Unit: membership validation (empty, duplicate name, mixed env, no common symbol); readiness aggregation over the health-state matrix; preview aggregation arithmetic including fees; WS scope intersection.
Contract: `listTradeGroups`, `previewTradeGroup`, `getTradeGroup` against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `TradeGroupUpdate` frames against the JSON schema `cv://ws/v1/trade_groups.schema.json` in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`.
Integration: preview across 5 accounts with mixed profiles and a recorded wallet/instrument fixture, asserting the exact per-leg numbers from the golden vectors in E28-T03.
Purity: transactional assertion that preview performs no writes and makes no exchange call.
Perf: preview p95 <=300 ms for 5 accounts with warm caches, measured in CI; WS projection sustaining 50 groups x 5 legs at the 100 ms throttle.
Coverage >=90%.

## Security notes
Asset A-09 (trade-group configuration, integrity 3). Threat **F1/Tampering - silently routing orders to an account the actor may not trade**: group membership is server-side truth and every read and preview re-intersects membership with the caller's grants, so a manager cannot preview or see a group containing accounts they were not granted. Threat **F4/Repudiation**: `tradegroup.preview` and `tradegroup.created|updated` are audited; membership changes carry a before/after diff. The mixed-environment guard is a safety control, not a convenience - it prevents a demo intent from reaching a live UID. Preview must remain side-effect free, or it becomes an unauthenticated-cost amplification vector; the rate limit bounds that cost. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
N/A directly, but the preview response is the data contract behind SCR-061's accessible table: every leg must carry a textual `status` and `reason`, never a colour code, and every skipped row must state its reason (SCR-061: "excluded rows always state the reason"). This shape is fixed here.

## Performance notes
Preview <=300 ms p95 (SCR-061). WS `trade_groups` throttle 100 ms with conflation (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS15.5). The projection must stay under SCR-062's client budget of 4 ms scripting per frame with 50 open groups x 5 legs, which constrains frame size: legs are sent as deltas, never as a full group re-send, except on the subscription snapshot.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_tradegroup_preview_seconds` histogram, `cv_tradegroup_preview_total{outcome}`, `cv_tradegroup_legs_skipped_total{reason}`, `cv_tradegroup_ws_frames_total`, `cv_tradegroup_members_gauge{group}`.
Audit: `tradegroup.created|updated|deleted|granted`, `tradegroup.preview` (who previewed what, for the repudiation trail).
Traces: one span per preview with a child span per leg.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T03** (the sizer the preview calls) and **E28-T02** (profiles to resolve). Consumes account health and key self-check state from **E27**, wallet snapshots from **E27**, instruments and fee rates from **E08**/**E27**, and the WS gateway and subscription-scope machinery from **E10**/**E17**. Its planner is consumed by **E34** (fan-out submission) and **E30** (order ticket).

## Branch
