title: Document profile and trade-group semantics and amend ADR-0008 with the shipped model
body:
## Context
E28 defines two contracts that five other epics consume: the per-account profile (E30 ticket, E34 fan-out, E35 rules, E39 risk caps, E41 journal attribution) and the trade group (E34, E41, E42). If the shipped behaviour drifts from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9 and ADR-0008 without the documents being updated, those epics will be built against a fiction. The Epic DoD requires exactly this: "Docs updated: relevant `docs/plan/2x-*` architecture/schema docs ... reflect final shipped behavior (not the original proposal) if they diverged during implementation."

There is also an operator-facing gap: nothing today explains to the owner how to choose a sizing rule, what a cap actually does at 00:00 UTC, what "2 of 3 ready" means, or how to recover a group whose membership is wrong. That is a runbook, not a docstring.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Amend `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md` with a "Shipped model (R3)" section recording: the final `profile_snapshot` contents, the skip-versus-failure taxonomy, the preview/planner sharing decision, and the mixed-environment guard. Record any deviation from the original decision explicitly, with the reason.
- Amend `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2 and SS9.3 where the implementation diverged (field names, defaults, the percent-versus-fraction convention, the `LegSizing` outcome type) - one PR, reviewed by the Architect.
- Amend `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4/SS3.3.2/SS3.3.3 if any column, constraint or index differs from the shipped migration.
- Write `docs/runbooks/profiles-and-trade-groups.md` covering: choosing a sizing rule with a worked example per mode; what each risk cap measures and when it resets; the reduce-only exemption matrix; readiness states and how to clear each one; how to fix a group with a wrong or mixed-environment membership; how to read a `profile.updated` audit diff; and what to do when a cap fires unexpectedly.
- Record ADR-0016 (from E28-K01) in the ADR index `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md`.
- Update `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` if any US-PROF story's screen or component list changed during implementation.
- A short "profiles for consumers" section in the backend package README naming the three entry points other epics may call (`get_effective_profile`, `size_leg`, `guard.check`) and stating that no consumer may re-derive size or re-implement a cap.

## Out of scope
User-facing help text inside the app (owned by the design tickets and the consuming stories); the security documentation set (E28-X01/X02).

## Acceptance criteria

title: Create and edit a per-account profile from the admin profiles list and editor
body:
## Context
Covers **US-PROF-001** ("Define a per-account profile", Must) and **US-PROF-002** ("Sizing rules", Must) as one vertical slice over **SCR-130 Admin: per-account profiles list** (`/admin/profiles`) and **SCR-131 Admin: profile editor**. These are RBAC-gated screens *inside the web app* - there is no separate admin application (owner decision, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).

SCR-130 is a table of one row per account showing leverage, sizing rule, SL/TP offsets, daily cap, max position and the allowed-symbol count, with a "changed since" diff column and an inline warning row for an account that allows all symbols ("(!) sub_002 allows all symbols - consider restricting"). SCR-131 is the editor, organised in the six sections the catalogue names: Leverage & margin, Sizing, Brackets, Risk caps, Symbols, Safety. Its accessibility rule is unusual and is a hard requirement: "every field has units and a worked example ('0.5% of 21 300 USDT ~= 106 USDT risk ~= 0.08 BTC at a 25-tick stop')".

Saving is a step-up-gated, fully audited action with a before/after diff (SCR-131: "`profile.updated` (step-up, full before/after diff)"), and the mandatory native-SL control is rendered as a floor that cannot be removed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-130** at `/admin/profiles` using CMP-001 Button, CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-106 ProfileBadge: one row per account, the "changed since" column driven by the profile revision projection, the all-symbols warning row, an empty state, and row actions (edit, duplicate/clone, delete) routing into their own flows.
- Unbound-account flagging: an account with no usable profile is shown as unable to trade until bound (SCR-130 sign-off: "unbound accounts are flagged (they cannot trade until bound)").
- **SCR-131** editor using CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-104 LeverageSlider, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-138 RiskCapMeter, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice - all six sections, wired to `GET`/`POST`/`PUT /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles[/{profileId}]`.
- Sizing section offering all four modes (fixed qty, fixed notional, % equity, risk-based) with mode-specific parameter fields and a rounding control, per US-PROF-002.
- **Live worked example** beneath the sizing section, recomputed from the account's current equity and the selected symbol's tick/lot filters, showing notional, quantity, implied risk in USDT and in R, and the resulting initial margin - the three numbers US-PROF-002's scenarios demand. Below-minimum-lot results show the minimum and offer it as a one-click choice.
- Field-level validation rendering from the E28-T02 error contract, with each message bound to its input via `aria-describedby`, including the exchange-limit messages ("SOLUSDT allows at most 20x - your 25x would be rejected").
- Safety section: `require_native_sl` rendered by CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice as a permanently-on floor with an explanation of why it cannot be disabled; the control is not a toggle that fails on save, it is visibly non-removable.
- Save flow: diff summary before save, step-up re-authentication, optimistic concurrency via `If-Match` with a "someone else saved version N - reload" recovery path, and an explicit "applies to future orders only" statement (SCR-131 sign-off checklist).
- Clone/duplicate of an existing profile into a new name on the same or another account.
- Analytics `profile.list_viewed`; audit surfaced back to the user as a "last changed by X at T" line.

## Out of scope
Templates (E28-S02); the symbol permissions matrix (E28-S02); trade groups (E28-S03, E28-S04); overrides (E28-S05); the backend routes and validation themselves (E28-T02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create a profile
  Given I open sub_001's profile editor
  When I set leverage cap, sizing rule, default SL and TP offsets, max risk per trade, max daily loss, max concurrent positions and allowed symbols, and save with step-up
  Then the profile is versioned and saved, and it is shown on every ticket targeting that account

Scenario: Invalid combination is explained on the field
  When the sizing rule is risk-based but no default stop distance or ATR source is defined
  Then saving is blocked, the message appears on the stop field itself, and it is associated with the input for screen readers

Scenario: Worked example follows the inputs
  Given equity is 21300 USDT and the stop is 25 ticks
  When I set risk-based sizing at 0.5%
  Then the worked example reads approximately 106 USDT risk and 0.08 BTC, and it updates within 300 ms of the last keystroke

Scenario: Below minimum lot offers the minimum
  Given the configured rule computes a quantity below the symbol's minimum order quantity at the current equity
  Then a warning states the minimum and offers it as a one-click choice

Scenario: Leverage above an allowed symbol's exchange maximum
  Given SOLUSDT is on the allowed list
  When I set leverage to 25x
  Then saving is refused with a message naming SOLUSDT and its 20x maximum

Scenario: The native stop-loss floor cannot be removed
  When I look at the Safety section
  Then the require-a-native-stop-loss control is shown as permanently on with an explanation, and no interaction can turn it off

Scenario: Editing a profile in use creates a new version
  Given open positions exist under the current profile version
  When I save an edit
  Then a new version is created, the open positions keep their originating version, and the screen states that the change applies to future orders only

Scenario: Concurrent edit is recovered, not lost
  Given another owner saved a newer version while my editor was open
  When I save
  Then I am told the version changed and offered a reload, and my unsaved values are not silently discarded

Scenario: Step-up is required
  When I save without a current step-up session
  Then I am prompted for password and TOTP, and the save completes only after it succeeds

Scenario: An account that allows all symbols is flagged
  Given sub_002's allowed list is empty
  When the profiles list renders
  Then its row carries a textual warning suggesting a restriction, expressed in text and not by colour alone

Scenario: A manager cannot edit an account they were not granted
  Given I am a manager without a grant on sub_002
  Then sub_002 is absent from my list, and navigating directly to its editor shows a permission error rather than a form
```

## Technical notes / design
The worked example is computed **client-side for responsiveness and re-verified server-side on save** - the client number is a preview, never an authority (SR-052). It calls the same arithmetic as E28-T03 through a thin TypeScript port that is validated against the E28-T03 golden vectors in a shared test fixture; any drift fails CI. This is the only permitted duplication of the sizing logic and it exists solely for keystroke latency.

The editor is a controlled form with a dirty-state guard on navigation. The diff summary before save is generated from the loaded version versus the current form state and is the same structure the audit event records, so what the user confirms is exactly what is audited.

Validation is two-layered to match the backend: synchronous shape validation on blur, and exchange-limit validation on save (or on an explicit "check limits" action), since the latter may require an instrument-cache refresh and cannot run per keystroke.

State handling: loading, loaded, dirty, validating, saving, save-failed (with the error code surfaced in plain language), version-conflict, forbidden.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): each section's field rendering and validation binding; worked-example computation against the shared golden vectors; dirty-guard; diff generation; version-conflict recovery.
Contract: the five profile operations consumed exactly as specified in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: create -> edit -> version bump -> list reflects "changed since", against a seeded database.
E2E (Playwright, added in E28-Q02): create a risk-based profile with step-up, see the worked example, attempt 25x on SOLUSDT and read the refusal, save, and see the new version on SCR-130.
A11y: axe-core clean on SCR-130 and SCR-131; manual screen-reader pass over the sizing section, the error bindings and the safety notice; keyboard-only completion of the whole form.
Visual regression on both screens in Storybook.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: **Tampering (O3)** - the form must never send a computed size or an effective cap; it sends the *policy*, and the server derives everything (SR-052). **Elevation of privilege** - the list and editor are RBAC-gated, but the gate is server-side; hiding a row is cosmetic only, and direct navigation to an ungranted account must show a permission error from a 403, not a client-side guess. **SR-025** step-up is enforced on save by the backend and surfaced by this UI - a UI that forgets to prompt still cannot save, by design. Every state-changing control is wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger so an audit row cannot be forgotten. No secret is ever displayed on these screens. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. SCR-131's own rule applies literally: **every field has units and a worked example**. Each validation message is bound with `aria-describedby` and the field is marked `aria-invalid`; the error summary at the top of the form is a `role="alert"` with in-page links to each offending field. The leverage slider (CMP-104) is operable by arrow keys with a text input alternative, and announces its value with its unit. The safety notice is a `role="note"` whose text explains the floor without relying on the lock icon. The profiles table follows CMP-049 keyboard semantics with a visible focus ring at >=3:1 contrast; the all-symbols warning is text, never a colour. The step-up dialog is a focus-trapped `role="dialog"` that returns focus to the save button on cancel. Layout survives 200% text scaling and 125% zoom; contrast >=4.5:1 for text in both themes.

## Performance notes
Worked-example recompute <=300 ms after the last keystroke (debounced 150 ms), matching the preview budget family in SCR-061. Save round-trip target <=2 s including server-side revalidation against exchange limits (SCR-131). The list is a small dataset and loads in one call; initial render within 300 ms of the API response. Profile changes propagate to open tickets within 2 s (SCR-130), using the transport decided in E28-K01.

## Observability
Analytics: `profile.list_viewed`, `profile.editor_opened`, `profile.sizing_mode_changed{mode}`.
Audit (server-side, surfaced here): `profile.created`, `profile.updated` with before/after, `profile.deleted`.
Frontend: error-boundary reports tagged with the screen ids SCR-130 and SCR-131; a metric for save failures by error code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.

title: Apply profile templates and manage the account-by-symbol permissions matrix
body:
## Context
Covers the remainder of **US-PROF-001** (templates as a way to define a profile) and **US-PROF-003** ("Allowed-symbol restriction", Must) on the UI side, over **SCR-132 Admin: profile templates** and **SCR-133 Admin: symbol permissions matrix**.

SCR-132's defining rule is that a template never writes directly: "Applying a template is a client-side prefill of SCR-131 - it never writes directly, so the user always sees and confirms the resulting profile." It ships built-in templates (conservative, standard, aggressive-demo-only) with their exact values, plus user-saved templates, and gates aggressive templates on live accounts behind an explicit acknowledgement.

SCR-133 is the bulk editor for the allow-list: a grid of accounts x symbols with allow/deny toggles, bulk row and column operations, and "a warning when a trade group's accounts have an empty symbol intersection" - which is the same rule E28-T05 enforces server-side when a group is saved. Its hardest constraint is a safety one: "denying a symbol with an open position is refused and recorded as `symbol_permission.change_refused`".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-132** modal using CMP-001 Button, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-049 Table, CMP-050 Card, CMP-087 AdminLayout: built-in templates with their exact values shown as readable summaries, user-saved templates with rename and delete, "save current profile as template", empty state.
- Apply flow: selecting a template **prefills SCR-131** and routes the user through the normal editor save (step-up, diff summary, validation) - there is no direct write path, and this is asserted by a test.
- Multi-account apply with a per-account preview of the resulting numbers before committing (roadmap E28 scope line: "profile simulation preview"), excluding accounts that would breach exchange limits and naming the reason (SCR-132 validation rule).
- Live-account guard: an "aggressive" template applied to a live account requires an explicit typed acknowledgement before the prefill proceeds.
- **SCR-133** at `/admin/symbol-permissions` using CMP-005 Checkbox, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger: virtualised grid over accounts x the listed USDT-perp universe, allow/deny cells with accessible names combining account and symbol, row and column bulk actions with confirmation, search/filter, and an unsaved-changes summary before save.
- Open-position guard: a symbol with an open position on that account is marked and cannot be denied; an attempt is refused with an explanation and recorded.
- Empty-intersection warning when the current selection would leave a defined trade group with no tradable symbol, naming the group.
- Bulk save as a single server call (SCR-133 performance rule), not one call per cell.
- Audit surfaced: `symbol_permission.changed`, `symbol_permission.bulk_changed`, `symbol_permission.change_refused`, `profile.template_applied`.

## Out of scope
The profile editor itself (E28-S01); backend validation (E28-T02); server-side order-path enforcement of the allow-list (E28-T04); trade groups (E28-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A template never writes directly
  Given I choose the "conservative" template for sub_001
  When I apply it
  Then the profile editor opens prefilled with the template's values, nothing has been saved, and I must confirm and step up to persist it

Scenario: Applying to several accounts previews each one
  Given I apply a template to Main, sub_001 and sub_002
  Then I see the resulting numbers per account before committing, and any account that would breach an exchange limit is excluded with a named reason

Scenario: Aggressive template on a live account
  Given the target account is live
  When I apply the aggressive-demo-only template
  Then I must acknowledge explicitly before the prefill proceeds

Scenario: Deny a symbol
  Given DOGEUSDT is allowed on account B and there is no open position in it
  When I deny it in the matrix and save
  Then the change is persisted in one call and audited, and a subsequent order for DOGEUSDT on account B is refused by the server

Scenario: A symbol with an open position cannot be denied
  Given account B holds an open ETHUSDT position
  When I attempt to deny ETHUSDT for account B
  Then the cell is marked as not deniable, the attempt is refused with an explanation, and the refusal is recorded

Scenario: Empty intersection is warned about before it breaks a group
  Given group Core3 contains accounts A and B
  When my pending changes would leave A and B with no symbol in common
  Then a warning names Core3 and states that the group could not trade anything

Scenario: Bulk row operation
  When I use "allow all" on one account's row and save
  Then one server call is made, the summary lists every added symbol, and the audit records a bulk change

Scenario: Unsaved changes are summarised
  Given I have toggled several cells
  When I press save
  Then a summary lists every addition and removal before the write is made

Scenario: The matrix is usable at full universe size
  Given six accounts and roughly four hundred listed symbols
  Then the grid renders within 600 ms and scrolls without jank, with row and column headers remaining visible
```

## Technical notes / design
The matrix is a virtualised grid (rows = accounts, columns = symbols, or transposed by a control) rendering only the visible window; header rows and columns are sticky. Cell state is a three-value model - allowed, denied, denied-and-locked (open position) - because a two-value checkbox cannot express the locked case accessibly.

Pending edits are held in a diff map (`{accountId: {symbol: allow|deny}}`) and submitted as one `PUT` of the resulting `allowed_symbols`/`blocked_symbols` arrays per touched account, through the existing E28-T02 profile route - no new endpoint is introduced. Accounts untouched by the edit are not written at all.

The empty-intersection check runs client-side against the loaded groups for instant feedback, and is re-checked server-side on save by E28-T05's validation; the client check is advisory only.

Templates are stored as local user preferences plus a set of built-ins compiled into the app; they are not profiles and never carry an account id, so a template can never leak a cap between environments.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): template prefill mapping per built-in; live-account acknowledgement gate; matrix diff-map construction; three-state cell rendering; empty-intersection detection.
Contract: the profile `PUT` used for bulk saves matches `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: bulk deny across two accounts resulting in exactly two `PUT` calls and the correct audit rows.
E2E (E28-Q02): apply a template through to a saved profile; deny a symbol and then watch the order path refuse it.
A11y: axe-core clean on both screens; manual screen-reader pass over the grid's cell naming and the locked-cell state; keyboard-only bulk operation.
Perf: 6 x 400 grid render <=600 ms, scroll without dropped frames, measured in the browser perf harness.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threat **SR-054 (allowed-symbol allow-list)** is the control this UI edits; because enforcement lives server-side in E28-T04, a client bug can lose a *restriction* visually but cannot grant trading rights - the server remains authoritative and that property is asserted by an E28-X03 test. The open-position deny guard exists so a permission change cannot strand an un-closable position. Bulk operations are wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and produce one audit row per account with the full added/removed lists (SR-064). Template values never cross environments. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-133's rule is explicit: "grid cells are checkboxes with accessible names combining account and symbol", and "allow/deny states are glyph + text, not colour alone". The locked (open-position) state is announced through `aria-disabled` plus a descriptive name explaining why. Sticky headers must remain associated with their cells via `aria-labelledby` so a screen reader in a virtualised grid still announces the right account and symbol. Bulk action buttons name their scope ("Allow all 412 symbols for sub_001"). The unsaved-changes summary is a focus-trapped dialog listing changes as text. SCR-132's template cards carry a readable summary of the settings they apply, and applying names the target account and lists what will change. Full keyboard operation including bulk actions; 200% text scaling and 125% zoom supported; contrast >=4.5:1.

## Performance notes
SCR-133: the matrix is virtualised; with 6 accounts and the full USDT-perp universe (~400 symbols) it renders in <=600 ms and scrolls without jank; bulk edits are a single server call. SCR-132: applying a template is a client-side prefill, so it has no server round-trip until the editor saves.

## Observability
Analytics: `profile.template_viewed`, `symbol_permission.matrix_viewed`.
Audit (server-side): `profile.template_applied{templateId, accountId}`, `symbol_permission.changed{accountId, symbol, allowed}`, `symbol_permission.bulk_changed{accountId, added, removed}`, `symbol_permission.change_refused`.
Frontend: error boundary tagged SCR-132/SCR-133; a metric for grid render time.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.

- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-S01** (the editor a template prefills and the matrix writes through) and **E28-D06** (signed-off handoff). Consumes the instrument list from **E08**, open-position state from **E29**, and group definitions from **E28-T05** for the intersection warning.

## Branch
`feat/e28-templates-and-symbols` - two PRs: (1) SCR-132 templates and prefill flow, (2) SCR-133 matrix, bulk actions and guards. Each <=400 LOC.

title: Define and manage trade groups with readiness, environment and symbol-intersection guards
body:
## Context
Covers **US-PROF-005** ("Create a trade group", Must) and the management half of **US-PROF-007** ("Trade-group lifecycle view", Must) over **SCR-062 Trade-group manager** (`/admin/trade-groups` for editing, with a read-only picker in the shell).

SCR-062 lists per group: "name, member accounts, default sizing basis, allowed symbols intersection, who may use it, armed-for-live flag". Its validation is the same rule set E28-T05 enforces server-side: ">=1 account; accounts must share at least one allowed symbol ('These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything.'); group names unique". US-PROF-005 adds the readiness display - "the group shows '2 of 3 ready' and orders fan out only to ready members, with the skip reported" - and the environment guard, "a trade group cannot mix Demo and Live".

The lifecycle *aggregate* view (aggregate size, average entry, uPnL, per-account expandable rows, group actions, divergence badge) is the other half of US-PROF-007 and depends on live positions, which arrive with **E29**/**E34**; this Story delivers the definition, listing and read-only projection, and the grid shell those epics fill in.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-062** at `/admin/trade-groups` using CMP-041 Menu, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard: list of groups with name, members, default sizing basis, the computed allowed-symbol intersection, who may use it and the armed-for-live flag; row expansion to per-account legs.
- Create/edit flow with CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect: name (unique), member selection with **per-account enable/disable** (the roadmap's "trade-group definition (named set of accounts) with per-account enable/disable"), and a live summary of the resulting symbol intersection.
- Environment guard in the UI: selecting accounts from two environments is refused at selection time with the message from US-PROF-005 ("a trade group cannot mix Demo and Live"), and the server refusal is surfaced identically if it is reached.
- Readiness strip per group: "N of M ready" with per-member textual reasons (key self-check failed, account disabled, locked out), refreshed from the `trade_groups` topic and the account health state.
- Empty-intersection refusal with SCR-062's exact copy, shown before save rather than after.
- Read-only group picker used by the shell and by the ticket's target selector, exposing the member count (US-PROF-005: "the group appears in the ticket's target selector with a member count").
- Live group rows subscribed to the `trade_groups` WS topic at its 100 ms throttle with 5 Hz UI coalescing, rendering group state as **text** and expanding to a nested per-account table (SCR-062 a11y rules).
- Degraded state: when an account's private WS is down the leg is shown as "state unknown for sub_002", never assumed (SCR-062 sign-off checklist).
- Group deletion with a confirmation naming the members, refused while the group has live legs.
- Audit surfaced as a "last changed by X at T" line; `tradegroup.created|updated|deleted|granted` are emitted server-side.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission, partial-failure remediation, retry and unwind (**E34**); flatten-group execution (**E34** - the button is rendered but wired to E34's single backend command, and is disabled with an explanatory reason until E34 lands); the fan-out ticket surface (E28-S04); aggregate PnL analytics (**E41**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create a group
  Given accounts A, B and C exist in the demo environment
  When I select all three and name the group "Core3"
  Then the group is saved and appears in the ticket's target selector with a member count of 3

Scenario: Mixed environments blocked at selection
  When I add a demo account and a live account to the same group
  Then saving is refused with "a trade group cannot mix Demo and Live", and the offending accounts are named

Scenario: Inactive member is reported, not hidden
  Given account B's key fails its self-check
  When I view the group
  Then it shows "2 of 3 ready", account B carries a textual reason, and the reason is available to screen readers

Scenario: Empty symbol intersection is refused before save
  Given account A allows only BTCUSDT and account B only ETHUSDT
  When I try to save them as one group
  Then I see "These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything." and nothing is written

Scenario: Duplicate name
  When I save a group whose name already exists
  Then the request is refused and the name field carries the error

Scenario: Per-account disable
  Given group Core3 has three members
  When I disable sub_002 within the group
  Then the group reports two enabled members, sub_002 remains a member, and the change is audited

Scenario: A group must have at least one account
  When I remove the last member and save
  Then saving is refused with a message stating that a group needs at least one account

Scenario: Degraded leg is stated, not assumed
  Given sub_002's private WS is down
  When the group row renders
  Then the leg shows "state unknown for sub_002" rather than a stale or assumed state

Scenario: Group state is text
  When any group row renders in either theme
  Then its state is readable as text and does not depend on a colour pill alone

Scenario: Scope is server-side truth
  Given I am a manager granted only account A
  When I open the group list
  Then I see only groups whose membership I am entitled to see, and a direct navigation to another group returns a permission error
```

## Technical notes / design
The group editor is a controlled form whose member selector re-derives the symbol intersection on every change by intersecting each member's effective allow-list (taking the empty list as "all listed symbols"). The derived intersection is advisory in the client and authoritative on the server (E28-T05), so the two must produce the same result - a shared fixture drives both test suites.

Group rows subscribe to `trade_groups` with `exchange_account_ids` scoped to what the user can see; the server intersects with grants, so the client never needs to filter. Frames arrive at a 100 ms throttle and are coalesced to 5 Hz before render (SCR-062 performance rule), and the grid is virtualised to stay under 4 ms scripting per frame with 50 open groups x 5 legs.

Flatten-group is rendered via CMP-123 FlattenAllButton but issues **one** backend command - "the UI never loops client-side over legs" (SCR-062). Until E34 ships that command, the button is present and disabled with a `disabledReason` naming the dependency, so the layout is final and only the wiring changes.

States: loading, empty, populated, editing, validation-blocked, saving, save-failed, degraded (one or more legs unknown), forbidden.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): intersection derivation including the empty-list case; environment guard; readiness aggregation; per-account enable/disable; virtualised row rendering; degraded-leg rendering.
Contract: `listTradeGroups`, `getTradeGroup` and the group create/update payloads against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `trade_groups` frames against the WS JSON schema.
Integration: create a group, disable a member, observe the audit row and the readiness recalculation.
E2E (E28-Q02): create Core3, break account B's key self-check in the fixture, and read "2 of 3 ready".
A11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass over the nested per-account table and the readiness strip; keyboard-only create and edit.
Perf: 50 groups x 5 legs at the 100 ms WS throttle staying under 4 ms scripting per frame, measured in the perf harness.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Asset A-09. Threat **Tampering - silently routing orders to an account the actor may not trade**: membership is server-side truth (US-PROF-005 NFR) and the client's view is a projection of what the server allows; a group containing an ungranted account is never returned. The environment guard is a safety control preventing a demo intent from reaching a live UID and is enforced in both layers deliberately - the UI guard is for clarity, the server guard is the control. Group edits are audited with before/after membership (SR-064). Every state-changing control is wrapped in CMP-093. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-062's rules apply literally: "The group list is a table with a row per group ...; group state is text, not a colour pill alone; expanding a group reveals a nested per-account table; every bulk action button names its scope ('Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912')." The readiness strip is text plus an `aria-live="polite"` region so a change from "3 of 3" to "2 of 3" is announced. Expansion controls use `aria-expanded` and the nested table is programmatically associated with its parent row. The degraded state is announced, not merely styled. Focus is preserved across WS-driven re-renders - a coalesced update must never steal or drop focus, which is an explicit test. Keyboard-only creation, editing and deletion; confirmation dialogs restate the exact member count; contrast >=4.5:1; 200% text scaling supported.

## Performance notes
Group state arrives on `trade_groups` and updates are coalesced to 5 Hz; the grid is virtualised and must stay under 4 ms scripting per frame with 50 open groups x 5 legs (SCR-062). Initial list render within 300 ms of the API response.

## Observability
Analytics: `tradegroup.manager_viewed`, `tradegroup.editor_opened`.
Audit (server-side): `tradegroup.created|updated|deleted|granted`.
Frontend: error boundary tagged SCR-062; metrics for frame scripting time and for WS reconnects on the `trade_groups` subscription.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

title: Show the per-account fan-out preview with per-leg sizing, exclusions and aggregate totals
body:
## Context
The roadmap's E28 scope line ends with "profile simulation preview ('this ticket would place X on A, Y on B')" - this Story delivers it, as the preview half of **SCR-061 Trade-group ticket (multi-account fan-out)**, serving **US-PROF-006**'s first scenario ("three per-account orders are created, each sized and levered by its own profile") in its pre-submission form.

SCR-061's wireframe fixes the table exactly: one row per account with `acct | profile | qty | lev | SL | ok`, a WARN row carrying its reason inline ("within 12% of daily loss cap"), an excluded row stating why ("sub_003 excluded: symbol not allowed by profile"), and the totals line ("total 0.430 BTC - 27,525 USDT - est. fee 1.9"). Its validation rules are equally specific: "every row must resolve a valid qty >= min lot ('sub_004 computes 0.0004 BTC, below the 0.001 minimum - excluded'); the group send is blocked if any included row lacks an SL; excluded rows always state the reason."

The split with **E34** is firm: this Story renders the preview and the send-blocking validation; E34 owns the actual send, the per-row live status, partial-failure remediation and the rate-limit budget indicator.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The SCR-061 preview surface using CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-100 PriceInput, CMP-101 QtyInput, CMP-102 SideToggle, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-107 OrderTicket, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-231 TifSelect, CMP-232 LimitsChip.
- Intent header: side, symbol, entry type and price, SL, TP and the risk basis selector, feeding `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`.
- Per-account preview table rendered from the E28-T05 response: account, profile name, computed qty, leverage, resolved SL and a textual status (ready / WARN with reason / excluded with reason), one row per member.
- Exclusion reasons rendered verbatim from the server's skip codes, mapped to the catalogue's copy: symbol not allowed by profile; below the minimum lot with the minimum stated; profile disabled; account locked out; account not ready.
- Aggregate totals line: total quantity, total notional and estimated fee, recomputed with the table.
- Per-row include/exclude checkbox and a per-row qty override that is **visibly exceptional** and flagged as an override (SCR-061 interactions; the override rules themselves come from E28-S05).
- Send-blocking validation, evaluated client-side for immediacy and re-evaluated server-side on send: the group send is blocked if any included row lacks an SL, or if any included row resolves an invalid quantity.
- Per-account DEMO/LIVE badge on every row (SCR-061 sign-off checklist) and a blocked state when the group contains an account in lockout.
- Debounced re-preview on every intent change - the endpoint is documented as "safe to call on every keystroke" and rate-limited, so the client debounces at 150 ms and cancels in-flight requests rather than queueing them.
- The `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` send affordance and `Esc` to cancel the preview, rendered and wired to E34's submit handler behind a feature flag; until E34 lands, send is disabled with a `disabledReason`.
- Empty and error states: no group selected, group has no ready members, preview failed (with retry), preview rate-limited (with the retry-after surfaced in plain language).

## Out of scope
Actual submission and per-row live status (queued -> sent -> accepted/rejected), partial-failure summary and remediation, the rate-limit budget indicator and the stagger control - all **E34**. The single-account ticket SCR-060 - **E30**. Override permission rules - **E28-S05**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preview resolves each account by its own profile
  Given group Core3 contains Main on risk 0.5% of equity, sub_001 on fixed 0.1 BTC and sub_002 on risk 0.5% of equity
  When I enter a BUY BTCUSDT limit at 64010 with a stop at 63900
  Then three rows appear with per-account quantity, leverage and stop, and the totals line sums them with an estimated fee

Scenario: Excluded rows always say why
  Given sub_003's profile does not allow BTCUSDT
  Then its row reads "excluded: symbol not allowed by profile" as text

Scenario: Below the minimum lot is excluded with the minimum stated
  Given sub_004 computes 0.0004 BTC against a 0.001 minimum
  Then its row states the computed quantity, the minimum and that it is excluded

Scenario: A warning does not exclude
  Given sub_002 is within 12% of its daily loss cap
  Then its row shows a warning with that reason in text and remains included

Scenario: Send is blocked without a stop on every included row
  Given one included row has no resolvable stop-loss
  Then send is disabled and the reason names the row

Scenario: Preview updates as the intent changes
  When I change the entry price
  Then the preview re-runs within 300 ms of my last keystroke and stale in-flight responses are discarded

Scenario: Preview never places an order
  Given I change the intent twenty times
  Then no order is created and no exchange call is made

Scenario: Rate limiting is explained, not silent
  Given previews exceed the server's per-user rate
  Then the surface shows a plain-language wait message with the retry time and keeps the last good preview visible

Scenario: A locked-out member blocks the group
  Given sub_001 is in lockout
  Then the surface shows the blocked state naming the account, and send is disabled

Scenario: Environment is unmistakable per row
  When the preview renders
  Then each row carries its own DEMO or LIVE badge as text, and the surface's environment badge is always visible
```

## Technical notes / design
The preview is entirely server-computed - the client renders the response and performs no sizing of its own. This is deliberate and is the point of SCR-061: what is previewed is exactly what the planner would send, because the same `plan_group` code produces both (E28-T05).

Request lifecycle: on any intent change, debounce 150 ms, abort the in-flight request, issue a new one with a monotonically increasing sequence number, and discard any response whose sequence is stale. A failed preview keeps the last good result on screen, marked stale, rather than blanking the table - a blank table during a fast market is worse than a labelled stale one.

Send-blocking validation is recomputed from the rendered rows so that it cannot disagree with what the user sees; the server repeats it on submit and the client's version is never the authority.

States: no-group, previewing, ready, stale, warn, blocked, rate-limited, failed.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): row rendering per status; exclusion-reason copy mapping for every skip code; totals rendering; send-blocking predicate; debounce and stale-response discarding; last-good-preview retention on failure.
Contract: `previewTradeGroup` request and `TradeGroupPreview` response against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: preview against a seeded five-account group with mixed profiles, asserting the rendered numbers equal the E28-T03 golden vectors.
E2E (E28-Q02): open the group ticket, enter an intent, see three ready rows and one excluded row with its reason, and confirm send is disabled when a stop is removed.
A11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass over the preview table and the send button's accessible name; keyboard-only operation including the send shortcut.
Perf: preview round-trip p95 <=300 ms for 5 accounts (SCR-061); render under 16 ms per update.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
The preview is a read-only surface and must remain one - a test asserts no mutating call is made from it. Threat **F2 (per-account profile ignored, so one account gets another's sizing)**: the client renders the server's per-leg attribution including the profile name used, which makes a mis-attribution visible rather than silent. Threat **O3 (Tampering)**: per-row quantity overrides are a hint only - the server re-derives and clamps (SR-052), and the override is flagged and audited (`tradegroup.row_overridden`). The per-row environment badge is a safety control against placing a demo-intended group on live. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-061's rules are explicit: "the preview is a table with row status in text; the send button names the account count; partial-failure summary is `role='alert'`". Every status - ready, warn, excluded, blocked - is text, never colour alone, and every excluded row states its reason in the row itself so a screen-reader user never has to hunt for it. The send button's accessible name includes the count ("Send group to 3 accounts"). Preview updates are announced through a polite live region summarising the change ("3 of 4 accounts ready, total 0.430 BTC") rather than announcing every cell. Focus is never stolen by a re-preview. The keyboard shortcut is discoverable in the button's tooltip and in the hotkeys settings screen. Contrast >=4.5:1; 200% text scaling supported; the table remains navigable at 125% zoom.

## Performance notes
Preview <=300 ms p95 for 5 accounts (SCR-061), with client debounce 150 ms on top. Render of a preview update <=16 ms so the surface never drops a frame while the user types. The preview endpoint is rate-limited server-side; the client must not exceed it under any typing speed, which the debounce plus abort guarantees.

## Observability
Analytics: `tradegroup.preview_opened`, `tradegroup.preview_intent_changed`.
Audit (server-side): `tradegroup.preview`, `tradegroup.row_overridden`.
Frontend: metric `cv_ui_preview_latency_ms` sampled per preview; error boundary tagged SCR-061; a counter for discarded stale responses so an over-eager client is visible in telemetry.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T05** (the preview endpoint and planner), **E28-S03** (group definition and the picker this surface consumes) and **E28-D06** (signed-off handoff). The send path, per-row live status and partial-failure UX are **E34**'s and are stubbed behind a flag here. title: Apply audited per-trade profile overrides that can narrow but never widen a risk cap
body:
## Context
Covers **US-PROF-008** ("Per-trade profile overrides", Should) across **SCR-061** (the per-row override in the fan-out preview), **SCR-114** (Trading defaults settings, where the user's own defaults are shown against the profile ceiling) and **SCR-132**. The story's three invariants are fixed and non-negotiable: an override "never widens a hard risk cap"; "the control is disabled with 'capped by profile'" when it would; and "given the ticket is submitted or cancelled, the override resets to the profile default for the next ticket". Its NFR adds: "each override is audited and journal-tagged".

The exact field-by-field rule set was the open question resolved by **E28-K01**, whose ADR-0016 this Story implements. The safety floor was fixed before that spike ran and does not depend on its outcome: no override may widen `max_position_notional`, `max_daily_loss`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage_cap`, the allowed-symbol set, or `require_native_sl`.

SCR-114 states the related rule for user defaults: "user defaults can never exceed the per-account profile limits set by the owner - the section shows each limit inline as a ceiling ('Your profile caps leverage at 10x')."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Override model and client state: a per-ticket override map applied on top of the effective profile, cleared on submit and on cancel, never persisted across tickets (US-PROF-008 scenario 3).
- Overridable-field enforcement per ADR-0016's decision table, implemented as data (a declarative table) rather than scattered conditionals, so the classification is auditable in one place and unit-tested field by field.
- Narrowing-only semantics: an override may reduce size, reduce leverage or tighten a stop; any attempt to widen is refused. Controls that could only widen are rendered **disabled with the reason "capped by profile"** (US-PROF-008 scenario 2) rather than allowed and then rejected.
- Server-side re-validation: the override travels as a hint on the preview and submit payloads and is re-derived and clamped by **E28-T04**'s guard and **E28-T03**'s sizer; a widening hint is clamped, recorded and reported back, never honoured.
- Override indication: an overridden row or field is visibly exceptional - a text marker naming what was overridden and its original value, per SCR-061 ("override is visibly exceptional" on the sign-off checklist).
- Audit and journal tagging: `tradegroup.row_overridden` and an order-level override tag carried into the journal so the trade is later identifiable as an override (US-PROF-008 NFR; **E41** consumes the tag).
- **SCR-114** ceiling display: each trading-default control shows its profile ceiling inline and refuses a value above it with the profile's wording.
- Reset affordance: "reset to profile default" per field and for the whole ticket, and an automatic reset on submit or cancel with a confirmation-free, announced transition.
- Mid-ticket profile-change behaviour exactly as decided in ADR-0016 (re-price, review state or block), implemented as specified there.

## Out of scope
Changing the profile itself (E28-S01); the rule engine's interaction with overrides (**E35**); journal analytics over override outcomes (**E41**); the submit path (**E34**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Allowed override
  Given the profile permits overriding size within its risk cap
  When I raise size for this ticket only, to a value still inside the cap
  Then the override applies to this order only and is recorded in the journal as an override

Scenario: Forbidden override is disabled, not rejected late
  When I try to raise leverage above the profile cap
  Then the control is disabled with "capped by profile" and never accepts the value in the first place

Scenario: Override expiry
  Given the ticket is submitted or cancelled
  Then the override resets to the profile default for the next ticket, and the reset is announced

Scenario: A crafted widening hint is clamped server-side
  When a request carries an override widening max position notional
  Then the server clamps to the profile cap, proceeds with the clamped value, records the clamp, and audits the attempt

Scenario: Every field is classified
  Given the override decision table from ADR-0016
  Then every field of AccountProfile has exactly one classification, and a unit test fails if a new field is added without one

Scenario: Overridden values are visibly exceptional
  Given a row's quantity is overridden
  Then the row states that it is overridden and names the original computed value

Scenario: Narrowing is always allowed
  When I reduce size, reduce leverage or tighten the stop
  Then the override is accepted, because it reduces risk

Scenario: Trading defaults cannot exceed the profile ceiling
  Given my profile caps leverage at 10x
  When I set a personal default of 20x in trading defaults
  Then it is refused with "Your profile caps leverage at 10x" and the ceiling is shown inline

Scenario: Mid-ticket profile change
  Given the owner edits the profile while my ticket is open
  Then the behaviour decided in ADR-0016 occurs, the ticket never silently uses stale sizing, and the change is surfaced within 2 seconds
```

## Technical notes / design
The decision table is a single declarative structure (`OVERRIDE_POLICY: dict[field, Literal["free","narrow_only","never"]]`) shared between the frontend (for control enablement) and the backend (for clamping) via the generated schema, so the two can never disagree. A test enumerates `AccountProfile.model_fields` and fails if any field is missing from the table - which is how a future field cannot silently become overridable.

"Narrowing" is defined per field with an explicit comparator rather than a generic less-than, because tightening a stop means moving it *closer* to entry while reducing size means a *smaller* number - the direction of safety differs by field and is encoded per entry.

Override state lives in the ticket's local store with an explicit lifetime, cleared by the same reducer that handles submit-success and cancel, so there is exactly one code path that can clear it and one that can set it.

The server treats an override as an upper-bound hint on the sizer's input, never as a replacement for the profile - the sizer signature is unchanged (E28-T03), and the clamp is recorded in the leg's explanation object.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): control enablement per classification; narrowing comparator per field; override lifetime across submit and cancel; ceiling display in SCR-114; overridden-row marker.
Unit (backend): clamping of a widening hint for every `narrow_only` field; rejection for every `never` field; the field-coverage test over the decision table.
Contract: the override payload shape on preview and submit against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: override applied end to end through preview, with the audit row and the journal tag asserted.
Security/abuse (feeds E28-X03): crafted payloads widening each protected cap, each asserting a clamp plus an audit row and no widened order.
E2E (E28-Q02): override size within the cap, submit, and confirm the next ticket starts from the profile default.
A11y: axe-core clean; screen-reader pass on the disabled control's reason and on the reset announcement.
Coverage >=90% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
This is the epic's most direct privilege-escalation surface: an override that widens a cap defeats SR-052, SR-053 and SR-054 in a single step. Two independent defences are required and both are tested - the client disables the control, and the server clamps regardless of what arrives. The "downward only" property is an automated test, not a convention (agreed in E28-K01). Every override is audited (`tradegroup.row_overridden`) and journal-tagged so an override can never be laundered into looking like normal policy. `require_native_sl` and the allowed-symbol set are classified `never` and a test asserts that classification explicitly by name, so a refactor cannot quietly reclassify them. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
A disabled control must state **why** it is disabled - "capped by profile" is rendered as visible text and exposed via `aria-describedby`, never as a tooltip alone, because a tooltip is unreachable by keyboard-only and touch users (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). The overridden state is text plus an optional glyph, never colour alone. Reset-on-submit is announced through a polite live region so a screen-reader user knows the ticket returned to defaults. The SCR-114 ceiling is part of each field's accessible description, so it is heard before the value is typed rather than after it is refused. Full keyboard operation; contrast >=4.5:1; 200% text scaling.

## Performance notes
Override application must not trigger a full re-preview beyond the existing 150 ms debounce; the recomputation stays inside SCR-061's <=300 ms preview budget. Mid-ticket profile changes surface within the 2 s propagation budget from SCR-130.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_override_applied_total{field}`, `cv_override_clamped_total{field}`, `cv_override_refused_total{cap}`.
Audit: `tradegroup.row_overridden{field, from, to}`, plus an audit row for every clamped widening attempt.
Journal: the override tag on the resulting order, consumed by **E41**.

## Dependencies

title: UX research: how the owner sets risk policy per account and thinks about fan-out
body:
## Context
E28 introduces five screens the product has never had - SCR-130 profiles list, SCR-131 profile editor, SCR-132 templates, SCR-133 symbol permissions matrix and SCR-062 trade-group manager - plus the preview half of SCR-061. All six express a mental model nobody has validated: that a trader thinks of "policy per account" as a durable object, and of a set of accounts as one tradable unit.

The risk of getting this wrong is concrete. SCR-131 requires "every field has units and a worked example" precisely because a sizing rule is abstract until it produces a number; if the worked example does not match how the owner reasons ("how much do I lose if this stop hits?"), the editor will be filled in wrongly and the resulting orders will be the wrong size. Equally, US-PROF-005's "2 of 3 ready" only makes sense if users expect a group to fan out partially rather than fail whole.

This is generative research ahead of wireframes, run two sprints before the wireframe ticket, consistent with the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-6 interviews: the owner (primary persona) plus account managers from `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, each 45 minutes, remote, recorded with consent.
- Topic guide covering: how risk per account is decided today (spreadsheet? habit? per trade?); which sizing rule is the default mental model and which is a fallback; what "max daily loss" means to them - realised only, or including open positions; whether a group is a saved thing or an ad hoc multi-select; expectations when one account of a group cannot trade; what makes an override feel exceptional rather than routine.
- Concept test of two alternative framings for the worked example: "risk in USDT" versus "risk in R", and whether both are needed simultaneously (US-PROF-002 asks for both).
- Card sort of the SCR-131 field set into the six proposed sections (Leverage & margin, Sizing, Brackets, Risk caps, Symbols, Safety) to validate the grouping before it is drawn.
- Findings report with themes, verbatim quotes, and a prioritised list of design implications, each tagged to the screen it affects.
- Explicit answers to three questions that block the wireframes: (1) is the profile list per account or per profile; (2) does a group need an armed-for-live flag distinct from the global arm control; (3) is the symbol matrix's default state allow-all or deny-all.
- A short research-debt note listing what was *not* answered and which later ticket must answer it.

## Out of scope
Any visual design, wireframe or prototype (E28-D02 onward); usability testing of built software (E28-Q04's exploratory charter covers that).

## Acceptance criteria
- At least four sessions completed and synthesised, including the owner.
- The three blocking questions each have a recorded answer with the evidence behind it, or an explicit "no signal - designer's call" with the reason.
- The card sort produces a section grouping that is either the proposed one or a documented alternative, and the chosen grouping is what E28-D02 draws.
- Findings are linked from the SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133 and SCR-062 entries in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Presented at a Design Review with the Chief Design Officer, the Owner and the consuming frontend lead present; decisions recorded in the ticket.

## Technical notes / design
Sessions use a paper-and-whiteboard protocol so participants are not anchored by an existing UI. The worked-example concept test uses two static cards with the same underlying numbers presented differently; order is counterbalanced across participants.

Consent and recording follow the same handling as E27-D01: no real API keys, UIDs or balances appear in any artefact, and recordings are stored in the project's research drive, not in the repository.

## Test plan
N/A - research, not software. Validity is protected by the counterbalanced concept test and by having a second researcher review the synthesis for interpretation bias.

## Security notes
No production data, keys or balances are shown or collected. Screenshots used as stimuli are synthetic. Recordings are Confidential and are retained only until the findings are signed off, then deleted; the deletion is recorded on the ticket.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session is run with a participant using keyboard-only navigation or a screen reader where available; if no such participant can be recruited, that gap is recorded as research debt and compensated by the dedicated a11y design review (E28-D05).

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Every state enumerated in the screen catalogue entry is drawn (empty, loading, error, populated, validation-blocked, partial-failure where applicable).

Follows **E27-D01** (accounts and key research) so the same participants are interviewed once about the whole admin area rather than twice. Its output blocks **E28-D02**.

Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

title: Wireframe SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and the SCR-061 preview with every state
body:
## Context
This is the structural design pass for every surface E28 introduces or changes. Each screen already has a catalogue entry in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` with its type, route, data sources, validation rules, states, components and a sign-off checklist - the wireframes must satisfy those entries rather than reinvent them, and where a wireframe departs from the catalogue, the catalogue is updated in the same PR.

Six surfaces are in scope: **SCR-130** (profiles list, `/admin/profiles`), **SCR-131** (profile editor, six sections), **SCR-132** (profile templates modal), **SCR-133** (symbol permissions matrix), **SCR-062** (trade-group manager, `/admin/trade-groups`) and the **preview half of SCR-061** (trade-group ticket) - the fan-out send, partial-failure and rate-limit states of SCR-061 belong to E34's design work and are explicitly excluded here to avoid two teams drawing the same screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Low-fidelity wireframes for all six surfaces, at desktop width first, with the density model from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- **Every state** enumerated by each catalogue entry, drawn - not described: loading, empty, populated, validating, error, forbidden, and each screen's specific states (SCR-130's unbound-account and allows-all-symbols warnings; SCR-131's validation-blocked and step-up states; SCR-132's live-account acknowledgement; SCR-133's locked cell with an open position and its unsaved-changes summary; SCR-062's degraded "state unknown for sub_002" and its N-of-M readiness; SCR-061's previewing, ready, warn, excluded, blocked and stale-preview states).
- SCR-131's worked example drawn as a first-class element, not a footnote, in the form the research chose (risk in USDT and in R), with its position relative to the sizing controls settled.
- SCR-131's Safety section drawing `require_native_sl` as a permanent floor - a control that visibly cannot be turned off, not a toggle that fails on save.
- SCR-133's grid drawn with sticky row and column headers, the three cell states (allowed, denied, denied-and-locked) distinguished by glyph and text, and the bulk row/column affordances.
- SCR-062 drawn with row expansion to per-account legs and the readiness strip.
- SCR-061's preview table drawn exactly to the catalogue's column set (`acct | profile | qty | lev | SL | ok`) with an inline WARN reason row and an excluded row stating its reason.
- Error and validation copy drafted for every rule named in the catalogue entries, including the exact strings the catalogue already fixes ("These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything.", "SOLUSDT allows at most 20x - your 25x would be rejected", "sub_003 excluded: symbol not allowed by profile").
- A component inventory per screen mapping every element to a CMP id from `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`, with any gap raised as a design-system contribution in E28-D03 rather than drawn as a one-off.
- Annotated flows: create profile, apply template, edit symbol permissions in bulk, create group, preview a fan-out.

## Out of scope
Hi-fi visual design, tokens and motion (E28-D03, E28-D04); SCR-061's send, partial-failure, retry and rate-limit states (**E34**'s design); SCR-060 single-account ticket (**E30**).

## Acceptance criteria
- All six surfaces wireframed with every catalogue-listed state drawn and labelled.
- Every element maps to an existing CMP id, or the gap is listed explicitly for E28-D03 to resolve with the design-system team.
- Error and validation copy exists for every validation rule listed in the six catalogue entries; no rule is left without a message.
- The wireframes are walked through with the backend lead to confirm every displayed value is actually available from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` - nothing is drawn that cannot be fetched.
- Reviewed at a Design Review with the Owner present; feedback resolved or logged.
- Any divergence from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is landed as an update to that document in the same change.

## Technical notes / design
The profiles list and the symbol matrix are two views of the same underlying allow-list; the wireframes must make the relationship obvious (a link from a row's symbol count to the matrix filtered to that account) rather than presenting them as unrelated screens.

The editor's two-layer validation (shape on blur, exchange limits on save) has a visible consequence: some errors appear immediately and some only on save. The wireframes must show how the later class is surfaced without feeling like a rejection out of nowhere - an explicit "check limits" affordance is one option to draw.

## Test plan
N/A - design artefact. Validation is the walkthrough with engineering and the Design Review sign-off.

## Security notes
No real account labels, UIDs, balances or keys appear in any frame - synthetic data only, matching the placeholder convention used in the catalogue. The step-up gate on save is drawn explicitly because a design that omits it invites an implementation that omits it. Screens must not display any secret; this is verified in copy review.

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes carry the accessibility annotations the catalogue demands: SCR-133's cells are checkboxes with names combining account and symbol; SCR-062's group state is text not a colour pill; SCR-061's row status is text and its send button names the account count; SCR-131's fields carry units and a worked example. Focus order is annotated per screen. Anything conveyed by colour has a text or glyph equivalent drawn alongside it, not promised for later.

## Performance notes
The wireframes must respect the performance constraints the catalogue states, because they are layout constraints: SCR-133's grid is virtualised over ~400 symbols, and SCR-062's grid is virtualised for 50 groups x 5 legs. A design that requires rendering everything at once is not acceptable.

N/A.

title: Hi-fi design and design-system contributions for the profile and trade-group surfaces
body:
## Context
The wireframes from E28-D02 become buildable specifications here. The six surfaces lean on a component set that is mostly existing (CMP-040 FormField, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-104 LeverageSlider, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard, CMP-138 RiskCapMeter, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-106 ProfileBadge, CMP-232 LimitsChip) but which several screens stretch: a virtualised matrix of checkboxes with sticky headers, a risk-cap meter that must read correctly at three different scales, and a safety notice that must communicate "this cannot be turned off" without looking like a broken toggle.

Anything the existing system cannot express is a **design-system contribution**, agreed with the design-system team and added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` - never an ad hoc one-off inside this epic (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS3.1: "any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi designs for SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and the SCR-061 preview, in light and dark themes, at the standard and compact densities defined in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- Tokens only - type scale, spacing, colour, elevation, radius - with no raw values anywhere; any missing token is raised as a design-system change rather than hard-coded.
- Design-system contributions, each with states, props, tokens, a11y contract and a Storybook specification: the symbol-matrix cell (three states: allowed, denied, denied-and-locked), the readiness strip ("N of M ready" with per-member reasons), the override marker used by SCR-061 and E28-S05, and any extension needed to CMP-138 RiskCapMeter and CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice.
- Final copy for every label, unit, helper text, validation message, empty state and confirmation, reviewed by the content reviewer and checked against the exact strings the screen catalogue fixes.
- The worked-example element specified to the number: format, precision, units, and how it renders while inputs are incomplete or the equity is unknown.
- Redlines: spacing, sizes, focus rings, hit targets (>=24x24 CSS px per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), and the responsive behaviour of the matrix and both grids.
- Per-row DEMO/LIVE badge treatment for SCR-061, and the environment treatment across the admin surfaces, consistent with CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal.
- Updates to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` and `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` for everything added or changed.

## Out of scope
Motion specification (E28-D04); the a11y review pass (E28-D05); the handoff pack (E28-D06); SCR-061's send and failure states (**E34**).

## Acceptance criteria
- Hi-fi frames exist for all six surfaces in both themes and both densities, covering every state drawn in E28-D02.
- Every new or extended component has a design-system entry with states, props, tokens and an accessibility contract, agreed with the design-system team, and is added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`.
- No raw hex, no ad hoc spacing, no off-scale type - verified by a token audit over the Figma file.
- Every screen's own "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is satisfied item by item and ticked in a comment on this ticket.
- Copy reviewed and approved; the fixed strings from the catalogue appear verbatim.
- Signed off by the Chief Design Officer and acknowledged by the frontend lead who will build E28-S01..S04.

## Technical notes / design
The risk-cap meter appears at three scales - a compact chip on the profiles list, a full meter in the editor, and a per-row indicator in the preview - and must remain legible and truthful at all three; the contribution specifies one component with a size prop rather than three lookalikes.

The safety notice communicating a non-removable floor is the hardest single piece of visual design in this epic: it must not read as a disabled control the user could enable with more permissions. The spec must therefore define its own visual language (a stated policy, not an input) and be user-tested informally with two participants before sign-off.

## Test plan
N/A - design artefact. The token audit and the checklist walkthrough are the verification.

## Security notes
The step-up gate and the audited-action affordance (CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger) are drawn on every state-changing control, so an implementation cannot omit them without visibly diverging from the spec. No frame contains a real key, UID, label or balance. The "aggressive template on a live account" acknowledgement is specified as a typed confirmation, not a single click, matching the danger-confirmation pattern in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast verified at >=4.5:1 for text and >=3:1 for non-text indicators and focus rings, in both themes, with the measurements recorded. Focus states designed for every interactive element including matrix cells and virtualised rows. Nothing is conveyed by colour alone - every status has text or a glyph. Hit targets >=24x24 CSS px. Layouts verified at 200% text scaling and 125% zoom. Disabled controls carry a visible reason, which is a design requirement here because E28-S05's "capped by profile" depends on it.

## Performance notes
The designs must be renderable inside the catalogue's budgets: SCR-133's virtualised grid over ~400 symbols in <=600 ms, SCR-062's grid under 4 ms scripting per frame at 50 groups x 5 legs, SCR-061's preview updating within 300 ms. Visual choices that would require per-cell shadows or per-row animation at those scales are rejected at design time, not discovered in QA.

title: Specify motion and state-transition choreography for profile saves, previews and readiness
body:
## Context
E28's surfaces change under the user's hands: a preview re-resolves as the intent is typed, a readiness strip flips from "3 of 3" to "2 of 3" when a key self-check fails, a save goes through step-up and returns a new version, and a matrix bulk action changes hundreds of cells at once. Without a specified choreography each of these will be implemented differently, and the fast-changing ones (preview, readiness) risk motion that distracts during trading or that violates reduced-motion preferences.

`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` defines the motion tokens; this ticket applies them and specifies what must *not* move.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion specification for: profile save (idle -> validating -> step-up -> saving -> saved/failed), preview recomputation (stale -> updating -> fresh, including the "keep the last good preview" transition), readiness change (N of M), matrix bulk apply and the unsaved-changes summary, group row expansion to legs, and the version-conflict recovery.
- Durations, easing curves and delays expressed **only** as tokens from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- An explicit "does not animate" list: numeric values in the preview table and the worked example do not tween between values (a tweening number is unreadable and, in a trading context, misleading); status text swaps without a transition; virtualised rows do not animate on scroll.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour specified per transition - each one either has a non-motion equivalent (an instant state change plus a text change) or is removed entirely.
- Loading and skeleton treatment for the two grids, specified so a re-render caused by a WS frame does not flash a skeleton.
- Focus-preservation rules across every transition: a coalesced WS update must never move or steal focus, and the version-conflict path must return focus to a sensible anchor.
- A prototype in Figma demonstrating the save flow and the preview refresh, for the handoff pack.

## Out of scope
Hi-fi visuals (E28-D03); implementation; SCR-061's send-in-progress and partial-failure choreography (**E34**).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every transition listed above has a specified duration, easing and trigger, all token-based.
- The "does not animate" list exists and explicitly includes preview numbers and the worked example.
- Every transition has a `prefers-reduced-motion` alternative, or is documented as removed under that preference.
- Focus-preservation rules are written per transition and are testable statements, not aspirations.
- The Figma prototype demonstrates the save flow and a preview refresh end to end.
- Signed off by the Chief Design Officer and the motion lead; acknowledged by the frontend lead.

## Technical notes / design
The preview refresh is the sensitive one: at a 150 ms debounce with a <=300 ms server round-trip, any transition longer than ~120 ms will still be running when the next update arrives. The specification therefore caps preview-related motion at the shortest token and prefers a state change with no motion at all, using a subtle staleness treatment instead of an animation.

Readiness changes are announced to screen readers through a live region (specified in E28-D05); the motion spec must not assume the visual transition is the only signal.

## Test plan
N/A - design artefact. Implementation conformance is checked in E28-D07 design QA, which includes a reduced-motion pass.

## Security notes
Motion must never be the sole indicator of a dangerous state. A blocked group, a refused save or a failed step-up is communicated by text and state, with motion at most as reinforcement - so a user with motion disabled loses no safety information.

## Accessibility notes
`prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured for every transition; no transition may flash more than three times per second (WCAG 2.2 2.3.1). Focus is never moved by an animation or by a data-driven re-render. Live-region announcements are coordinated with, not replaced by, the visual transition. Skeletons must not be announced as content changes.

## Performance notes
Motion must not compete with the render budgets: the group grid stays under 4 ms scripting per frame at 50 groups x 5 legs, so no per-row transition is permitted at that scale. Animations are composited transforms and opacity only - no layout-triggering properties.

N/A.
