title: Accessibility design review of the six profile and trade-group surfaces
body:
## Context
Two of E28's surfaces are accessibility-hard in ways that must be solved at design time rather than discovered in an audit. **SCR-133** is a virtualised grid of checkboxes across accounts x ~400 symbols where each cell's accessible name must combine account and symbol and where one cell state means "you cannot deny this, there is an open position". **SCR-061**'s preview is a live-updating table whose every status must be text, whose send button must name the account count, and which must not steal focus while a user types.

`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA. The catalogue entries already carry per-screen a11y rules; this review checks the hi-fi designs against them before a line of code is written, because retrofitting an accessible name onto a virtualised grid is far more expensive than designing it in.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Review of the E28-D03 hi-fi frames for all six surfaces against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` and each screen's catalogue a11y notes.
- Contrast measurements recorded for every text and non-text indicator in both themes, including the three matrix cell states, the readiness strip, the WARN and excluded row treatments and every focus ring.
- Focus-order diagrams per screen, including the modal flows (step-up, unsaved-changes summary, template acknowledgement, delete confirmation) and the return-focus target for each.
- Accessible-name specification for every non-obvious control: matrix cells (account + symbol + state), bulk row and column actions (naming their scope and count), the send button (naming the account count), expansion controls, and the reset-to-default affordances.
- Live-region plan: what is announced, with which politeness, on readiness change, preview refresh, save result, bulk-apply result and degraded-leg transitions - deliberately limited so a fast-updating preview does not flood a screen reader.
- Disabled-control reason specification: every disabled control states why in visible text exposed via `aria-describedby` - required by E28-S05's "capped by profile" and by SCR-061's exclusion reasons.
- Keyboard-operation specification for the matrix (arrow navigation, range selection, toggling, bulk actions) and for both grids, with no mouse-only path anywhere.
- Text-scaling and zoom verification at 200% and 125% with screenshots, especially for the two grids.
- A findings list with severity, each either resolved in the designs before sign-off or logged with an owner and a date.

## Out of scope
Automated axe-core runs against built code and manual screen-reader passes on the implementation (**E28-Q04**); the design QA of the built screens (**E28-D07**).

## Acceptance criteria
- All six surfaces reviewed with findings recorded, and every Critical or High finding resolved in the designs before sign-off - not deferred to implementation.
- Contrast measurements recorded for both themes, with no value below 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for non-text indicators and focus rings.
- Focus-order diagrams exist for every screen and every modal, including return-focus targets.
- Every matrix cell state, every row status and every disabled control has a specified accessible name and reason.
- The live-region plan is written and bounded - a specified maximum announcement rate for the preview surface.
- Signed off by the accessibility specialist and the Chief Design Officer.

## Technical notes / design
For the virtualised matrix, the review must settle whether the grid is exposed as a `role="grid"` with `aria-rowindex`/`aria-colindex` on the rendered window, or as a set of labelled checkboxes with an off-screen description - and the decision is recorded with its rationale, because it determines the DOM structure E28-S02 builds.

The preview's announcement rate is capped by announcing a *summary* ("3 of 4 accounts ready, total 0.430 BTC") rather than per-cell changes, at most once per second, with the full table available on demand through normal table navigation.

## Test plan
N/A - design review. The findings become test cases in E28-Q04's a11y audit, so nothing found here can be lost.

## Security notes
Accessible alternatives must not weaken a safety control: the step-up dialog remains a real gate for keyboard and screen-reader users; the "aggressive template on live" typed acknowledgement is not reduced to a single keypress; the non-removable native-SL floor is announced as policy, never as a control the user might be able to change.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility work; its own DoD is the checklist above. It covers WCAG 2.2 AA including the 2.2-specific criteria that matter here: focus appearance (2.4.11), target size minimum (2.5.8), consistent help (3.2.6) and redundant entry (3.3.7) - the last two matter for the repeated step-up prompts across profile, template and matrix saves.

## Performance notes
Accessible-name computation for a virtualised grid must not require rendering every cell; the chosen approach is checked against SCR-133's <=600 ms render budget in the review itself.

N/A.

## Context
The design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` is absolute: "no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off (Status 'Done' on the design ticket)". E28-S01 through E28-S05 all declare this ticket as a blocker, so it is the gate that releases the epic's frontend work. It must therefore be genuinely complete - a pack a developer can build from without asking a question.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A single handoff pack covering SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and the SCR-061 preview, linked from every consuming story.

- Final copy deck: every label, unit, helper text, validation message, empty state, warning and confirmation, as a table keyed by the error code or state it belongs to - so the frontend maps a server error code straight to a string with no invention.
- Data-binding notes per element: which API field or WS frame field supplies it, quoting `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, including what to render when the field is absent or stale.
- The design-system contributions from E28-D03 confirmed as merged into the system with Storybook entries, so a story does not have to build a system component itself.
- An open-questions list, each with an owner and a decision date, and a statement that none of them blocks implementation.
- A walkthrough session with the frontend engineers who will implement E28-S01..S05, recorded, with questions answered in the pack rather than in chat.
- Confirmation that the catalogue documents (`14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`) now match the pack.

## Out of scope
Design QA of built screens (E28-D07); any new design exploration - this ticket assembles and signs off, it does not redesign.

## Acceptance criteria
- The pack is complete for all six surfaces, with no "TBD" in any state, copy string or binding note.
- Every server error code that the six screens can receive (from E28-T02 and E28-T05: `validation_failed`, `native_stop_mandatory`, `conflict`, `precondition_failed`, `step_up_required`, `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `env_mismatch`, `rate_limited`, `profile_forbidden`, `risk_limit_breached`) has a user-facing string in the copy deck.
- Every design-system contribution is merged with a Storybook entry before this ticket closes.
- The walkthrough has happened and its questions are answered inside the pack.
- Signed off by the Chief Design Officer; accepted in writing by the frontend lead; Status Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming stories start (S16), i.e. by the end of S14.

## Technical notes / design
The copy deck is keyed by error code rather than by screen, because the same code can surface on several screens and must read identically everywhere. Where a server message already carries a specific string (for example the exchange-limit message naming a symbol and its maximum leverage), the deck records that the server string is rendered verbatim and the client adds no wrapper text.

## Test plan
N/A - the acceptance of the pack by the frontend lead is the verification. Its completeness is retested implicitly in E28-D07, where any gap shows up as a build discrepancy.

## Security notes
The pack states, per screen, which actions require step-up and which emit audit events, so the implementation cannot omit them silently. It contains no real credentials, UIDs, labels or balances. It also records the rule that no secret is displayed on any of these screens, to be verified in copy review.

## Accessibility notes
The pack carries E28-D05's outputs in full - focus orders, accessible names, live-region plan, disabled-control reasons, contrast measurements - so a developer never has to infer them. Any a11y finding still open is listed with an owner and must not be Critical or High.

## Performance notes
The pack restates the per-screen budgets (SCR-133 <=600 ms grid render, SCR-062 <=4 ms scripting per frame, SCR-061 <=300 ms preview, SCR-131 <=2 s save) so they are visible to the implementer rather than buried in the catalogue.

## Observability
The pack lists the analytics and audit events each screen must emit (`profile.list_viewed`, `profile.template_applied`, `symbol_permission.changed`, `tradegroup.preview`, and the audited `profile.*` and `tradegroup.*` events), so instrumentation is part of the build rather than a follow-up.

title: Design QA the implemented profile and trade-group screens against the handoff pack
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS3.2 makes design QA a default-on gate for net-new UI stories: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set." E28 ships five net-new admin surfaces plus a preview surface, so this pass is required before the epic can close.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen-by-screen comparison of the built SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and SCR-061-preview against the E28-D06 handoff pack, in both themes and both densities.
- State-by-state verification: every state in the pack is reachable in the build and matches - including the ones that are awkward to reach (validation-blocked, version conflict, step-up prompt, locked matrix cell, degraded leg, stale preview, rate-limited preview, blocked group). Where a state cannot be produced by normal interaction, it is forced with a fixture, and the fixture is committed.
- Token audit of the built code: spacing, type scale, colour, radius and elevation come from tokens, with no raw values - checked by inspecting computed styles, not by eye.
- Copy verification against the copy deck, including that server-supplied strings are rendered verbatim and that every error code maps to the agreed string.
- Motion verification including a `prefers-reduced-motion` pass, and confirmation that preview numbers and the worked example do not tween.
- Focus-order and focus-preservation verification against the pack's diagrams, including that a WS-driven update never steals focus.
- Contrast spot-checks on the built screens in both themes.
- Discrepancy log, each item either fixed within the epic or filed as a Bug with a priority and an owner.
- A sign-off comment recording the result per screen.

## Out of scope
Functional testing (E28-Q01..Q05); the accessibility audit proper (E28-Q04) - this pass checks design conformance and flags a11y regressions it happens to see, rather than replacing the audit.

## Acceptance criteria
- All six surfaces reviewed in both themes and both densities, with a per-screen verdict recorded.
- Every state in the pack has been observed in the build, with a committed fixture for any state that needed forcing.
- The token audit finds no raw values; any found are fixed, not waived.
- The reduced-motion pass is clean and the no-tweening rule holds for every numeric display.
- Discrepancies are all either fixed or filed with a priority, and none of the open ones is P0 or P1.
- Sign-off comment posted by a designer or a design-system-trained reviewer, and referenced by E28-S01..S04 and by the epic.

## Technical notes / design
Review runs against the staging build on the R3 demo environment with a seeded fixture set: six accounts, four profiles including one with an empty allow-list, two trade groups including one with a failing key self-check, and one account holding an open position so the matrix's locked cell is reachable. The fixture is the same one E28-Q01 builds, so QA and design QA look at identical data.

## Test plan
The comparison itself is the test. Evidence is screenshots per screen and state, attached to the ticket; the token audit is evidenced by computed-style dumps rather than screenshots.

## Security notes
The review confirms that every state-changing control in the build actually routes through the step-up gate and emits its audit event as the pack specifies, and that no screen displays a secret. A missing step-up prompt is a P0 discrepancy, not a cosmetic one, and is escalated to E28-X02 rather than merely logged.

## Accessibility notes
Focus rings, focus order, disabled-control reasons, accessible names on matrix cells and bulk actions, and live-region behaviour are all checked against the pack. Any regression is filed with `a11y` and fed to E28-Q04. The reduced-motion pass is part of this ticket.

## Performance notes
The reviewer confirms the built screens meet their stated budgets under the fixture load - SCR-133's grid render, SCR-062's grid scripting time and SCR-061's preview latency - using the browser performance panel, and files a `perf`-labelled Bug for any breach.

## Observability
The reviewer confirms that the analytics and audit events listed in the pack are actually emitted, by observing them in the dev tools network log and the audit browser.

title: Write the black-box test plan and fixture set for profiles, sizing and trade groups
body:
## Context
E28 decides how large every order in the system will be. A sizing bug here does not produce a wrong pixel; it produces a position ten times too large on five accounts at once. The testing strategy (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`) requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review, and the R3 quality gates require recorded fixtures for partial fills, rejections, rate limits and disconnects.

This ticket writes the plan and builds the fixtures **before** the features land, so the stories are implemented against an agreed definition of correct rather than a post-hoc one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Black-box test plan at `qa/plans/e28/test-plan.md`, organised by story group: profile definition and sizing (US-PROF-001, US-PROF-002), symbol restriction (US-PROF-003), risk caps (US-PROF-004), trade groups (US-PROF-005, US-PROF-007 definition half), preview (roadmap's simulation-preview scope line), overrides (US-PROF-008).
- One test case per Gherkin scenario across all eight US-PROF stories, each with preconditions, steps, expected result and the evidence to capture - traceable back to the scenario id so coverage is provable.
- Boundary case catalogue, derived from the DDL and the sizing algorithm: leverage at 1, 100 and 101; `max_open_positions` at 1, 50 and 51; `slippage_tolerance_bps` at 0, 1000 and 1001; `max_orders_per_minute` at 1, 600 and 601; TP ladder summing to exactly 100 and to 100.000001; quantity exactly at the minimum lot and one step below; daily loss exactly at the cap; an intent at 00:00:00 UTC on the rollover boundary.
- Negative and hostile case catalogue: `require_native_sl = false` by every route; a crafted order for a non-allowed symbol; an oversized quantity hint; a group mixing demo and live; a preview attempting to mutate; a manager acting on an ungranted account; an override widening each protected cap.
- **Fixture set** committed under `tests/fixtures/e28/`: six exchange accounts (one main, five subs; four demo, two live), four profiles covering all four sizing modes including one with an empty allow-list and one with a TP ladder, two trade groups (one healthy, one with a failing key self-check), one account holding an open position so the matrix's locked cell is reachable, and a recorded `instruments-info` snapshot for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT and DOGEUSDT with their real tick, lot, min-notional and max-leverage values.
- Shared golden sizing vectors agreed with E28-T03 so QA and engineering assert the same numbers - QA owns an independent recomputation of at least ten of them by hand, to catch an algorithm that is self-consistently wrong.
- Exploratory charters (session-based, 90 minutes each): "sizing rules under extreme equity", "the profile editor under exchange-limit conflicts", "trade-group membership edge cases", "preview under rapid intent changes".
- Entry/exit criteria and a defect-triage convention for the epic.

## Out of scope
Writing the automation (E28-Q02); load, soak and chaos runs (E28-Q03); the a11y audit (E28-Q04); security abuse cases (E28-X03 - though the hostile catalogue here feeds it).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every Gherkin scenario in US-PROF-001..008 maps to at least one written test case; a coverage table proves it with no gaps.
- The boundary and hostile catalogues exist and each entry names the constraint or control it probes.
- The fixture set is committed, loads into a clean database with one command, and is used by E28-Q02, E28-D07 and E28-X03 - verified by at least one of them consuming it before this ticket closes.
- Ten golden sizing vectors are independently recomputed by QA and match the engineering values exactly; any mismatch is raised as a Bug before the sizer merges.
- Entry/exit criteria and the triage convention are agreed with the Owner and the Architect.
- The plan is reviewed by the second QA/SDET.

## Technical notes / design
The independent recomputation is the point of this ticket, not a formality: it is the only step in the whole epic where the sizing arithmetic is derived twice from the story text rather than once from the code. It is done in a spreadsheet from US-PROF-002's stated inputs, and the spreadsheet is committed alongside the vectors.

Fixtures are expressed as SQL seeds plus JSON API-response recordings, never as live exchange calls, so the suite is deterministic and runnable offline.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan. Its own verification is the coverage table and the peer review.

## Security notes
Fixtures contain no real API keys, UIDs, labels or balances - all synthetic, with keys that are structurally valid but non-functional, checked by the secrets scanner over `tests/fixtures/`. The hostile case catalogue is shared with the Security engineer and becomes the basis of E28-X03's abuse-case suite, so the two are not written twice with different assumptions.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the a11y acceptance points from the screen catalogue as explicit test cases (text status chips, accessible names on matrix cells, disabled-control reasons), which E28-Q04 then executes in depth.

## Performance notes
The plan states the per-surface budgets as testable assertions (preview <=300 ms, save <=2 s, matrix render <=600 ms, guard <=5 ms p95, fan-out overhead <=50 ms + <=10 ms/account) and names which ticket measures each.

## Observability
The plan lists the metrics and audit events each scenario should produce, so a test can assert on telemetry as well as on the response - in particular that every refusal produces an audit row.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario of the covered stories is mapped to an executed test case with a pass/fail result recorded on the story.

- [ ] Coverage of the epic's acceptance criteria reported in the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

Blocked by **E28-T01** (the schema the fixtures are built against). Feeds **E28-Q02**, **E28-Q03**, **E28-Q04**, **E28-X03** and **E28-D07**.

title: Automate the profiles, symbol-permission and trade-group E2E suite in Playwright
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` puts E2E at the top of the pyramid and the R3 quality gates require "Playwright web + Electron covering ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, bracket, fan-out, rule creation in both editors, alert firing, journal capture". E28 owns the profile and trade-group portions of that suite, and the suite is what protects the sizing path from silent regression once E30, E34 and E35 start consuming it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright suite under `tests/e2e/e28/`, running against the R3 demo staging environment with the E28-Q01 fixture set, in both the browser and the Electron shell.
- Journeys automated:
  1. Create a risk-based profile through SCR-131 with step-up, observe the worked example, save, and see the row on SCR-130 with its "changed since" value.
  2. Attempt 25x leverage with SOLUSDT allowed and assert the refusal names the symbol and its 20x maximum.
  3. Attempt to disable the native stop-loss and assert it cannot be done from the UI, and that a direct API call is refused with `native_stop_mandatory`.
  4. Edit a profile that has an open position and assert a new version is created while the position keeps its originating version.
  5. Apply a template through SCR-132 and assert it prefills the editor without writing, then save through the normal path.
  6. Deny a symbol in SCR-133, save in one call, then assert an order for that symbol on that account is refused with 403.
  7. Attempt to deny a symbol with an open position and assert the refusal and the recorded event.
  8. Create a group in SCR-062, break one member's key self-check in the fixture and assert "2 of 3 ready" with a textual reason.
  9. Attempt a demo+live group and assert the refusal.
  10. Open the SCR-061 preview, enter an intent, assert three ready rows sized by their own profiles plus one excluded row with its reason, and assert send is disabled when a stop is removed.
  11. Apply an in-cap override and assert it is marked, applied and reset after cancel.
- Concurrency journey: two browser contexts editing the same profile, asserting the version-conflict recovery path rather than a lost update.
- Deterministic control of time for the daily-loss rollover journey via a clock-injection fixture, so the boundary is testable without waiting.
- Stability work: no arbitrary sleeps, explicit waits on state, and the suite green three consecutive runs before it is accepted.
- Wiring into CI as a required check for the E28 paths, with traces and video retained on failure.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission journeys and partial-failure remediation (**E34**'s suite); load and chaos (E28-Q03); the a11y audit (E28-Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
- All eleven journeys plus the concurrency journey are automated, pass against staging, and are green on three consecutive CI runs with zero flakes.
- Each journey asserts the user-visible outcome **and** the audit row it must produce, so a silently unaudited action fails the test.
- The suite runs in both the browser and Electron, with any Electron-specific divergence documented.
- Failure artefacts (trace, video, console log) are retained and attached automatically.
- The suite is a required check on the E28 code paths.
- Total runtime under 12 minutes so it does not become a merge bottleneck.

## Technical notes / design
Tests drive the UI and assert through the UI, with two exceptions that are deliberate: audit assertions read the audit API, and the "direct API call is refused" steps issue an HTTP request outside the browser context. Both exceptions are documented in the suite README so the black-box boundary is an explicit decision rather than a drift.

Step-up is handled with a deterministic TOTP seed in the staging fixture, so the second factor is scriptable without weakening the production path.

Each journey seeds and tears down its own data from the shared fixture, so journeys can run in parallel without ordering assumptions.

## Test plan
Self-verifying. Suite health is tracked by a flake-rate metric in CI; any test flaking more than once in twenty runs is quarantined and fixed rather than retried.

## Security notes
The staging TOTP seed and fixture keys are non-production, structurally valid but non-functional, and are stored as CI secrets rather than in the repository. The suite deliberately includes negative security journeys (native-SL disable, denied-symbol order, ungranted-account access), and those assertions are duplicated in E28-X03's suite so a deletion here does not silently remove the control's coverage.

## Accessibility notes
Every journey is driven through accessible selectors - roles and accessible names, never CSS classes or test ids where a role exists - so a regression that breaks an accessible name breaks the test. This is a deliberate, low-cost accessibility regression net underneath the dedicated audit in E28-Q04.

## Performance notes
The suite asserts the user-visible budgets it can observe reliably: preview updates within 300 ms of the last input and the save completing within 2 s, both measured with generous tolerance in CI and reported as a trend rather than a hard gate (the hard gates live in E28-Q03).

## Observability
Each run publishes pass/fail counts and duration to the CI dashboard; failures link to the trace. Audit assertions double as a check that the observability described in the stories is actually emitted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario of the covered stories is mapped to an executed test case with a pass/fail result recorded on the story.

- [ ] Coverage of the epic's acceptance criteria reported in the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-Q01** (plan and fixtures) and by **E28-S01** and **E28-S03** (screens to drive). Journeys 10 and 11 additionally need **E28-S04** and **E28-S05** and are landed as those merge.

title: Run the performance, load and chaos scenarios for sizing, the risk guard and group preview
body:
## Context
Three hard numbers in this epic are budgets, not aspirations: the risk guard adds **<=5 ms p95** to the order path (US-PROF-004 NFR), the fan-out preview returns in **<=300 ms** for five accounts (SCR-061), and backend-added fan-out overhead is **<=50 ms + <=10 ms per additional account p95** (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` SS5.2, budget #4 fan-out sub-clause). All three sit inside the R3 hard gate of order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms.

The chaos requirement is equally concrete: the risk guard keeps in-memory counters, so a restart or a WS disconnect must not reopen a breached cap. R3's chaos gate demands "backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out - all resume to a correct, reconciled state"; the profile-owned part of that is counter reconstruction.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6/Locust scripts under `tests/load/e28/` for: `POST /trade-groups/preview` at five accounts sustained for 10 minutes; the risk guard exercised through the OMS submit path at the per-UID order rate across five accounts for one hour; profile save under concurrent editors.
- Micro-benchmark harness for `size_leg` and `guard.check` run in CI on every change to those modules, with a regression threshold that fails the build on a slowdown beyond the agreed tolerance.
- Measurement and recording of: guard p95 and p99 with warm and cold caches; preview p50/p95/p99 at 1, 3, 5 and 20 member accounts (20 being the Business-KYC ceiling); the per-account marginal cost, to verify the <=10 ms/account slope rather than only the 5-account point.
- Soak: the `trade_groups` WS projection at 50 groups x 5 legs for 60 minutes, asserting the 100 ms throttle holds, memory is flat and no frame is lost.
- Chaos scenarios, each with a defined correct outcome:
  1. Backend restart with a breached daily-loss cap - the cap must remain breached after the counters rebuild, and an entry attempted during the rebuild window must be refused, not permitted.
  2. Private WS disconnect and reconnect mid-session - counters reconcile from Postgres and no double-count occurs.
  3. Postgres becoming unavailable during a guard evaluation - the guard fails **closed** and raises the alert.
  4. Instrument cache unavailable during a profile save - the save is refused with `instrument_cache_unavailable` and a `Retry-After`, never saved unvalidated.
  5. Clock skew of +/-90 seconds across the 00:00 UTC rollover - the daily accumulator resets exactly once.
- A results report with the numbers, the environment they were measured on, and a pass/fail against each budget; regressions filed as `perf`-labelled Bugs.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission load and the rate-limit governor (**E34**); engine FPS work; the 7-day R3 soak (`q09` in the roadmap).

## Acceptance criteria
- Guard evaluation p95 <=5 ms with a warm cache, measured over at least 10 000 evaluations; the cold-cache number is recorded separately and documented rather than hidden.
- Preview p95 <=300 ms at 5 accounts, and the marginal per-account cost is measured and reported against the <=10 ms/account slope.
- The `trade_groups` projection soaks for 60 minutes at 50 groups x 5 legs with flat memory and no lost frames.
- All five chaos scenarios produce their defined correct outcome; scenario 1 and scenario 3 are treated as safety-critical and a failure in either blocks the epic.
- The micro-benchmark harness is wired into CI with a regression threshold.
- Results are recorded in the report and referenced from E28-Q05 and from the epic.

## Technical notes / design
Measurements are taken on the R3 staging topology over Tailscale, matching the network assumption in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` SS4 - the Bybit RTT component is excluded from the backend-internal budgets and reported separately, per that document.

The marginal-cost measurement matters more than the headline: a preview that is fast at five accounts but quadratic in member count would pass a naive test and fail at twenty. Member counts are therefore swept, and the fitted slope is what is reported.

Chaos scenario 1 is run by killing the process rather than by a graceful shutdown, so the rebuild path is genuinely exercised.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test. Its own reliability comes from running each measurement three times and reporting the median with the spread, and from pinning the staging environment's resources so runs are comparable across weeks.

## Security notes
Fail-closed behaviour is a security property, not just a reliability one: scenario 3 verifies that a database outage cannot become a path to unguarded orders. Scenario 1 verifies that a restart cannot clear a lockout - which would otherwise be an availability-shaped privilege escalation. Both results are reported to the Security engineer for E28-X04. Load scripts use synthetic accounts on demo only and never touch a live UID.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend load and chaos.

## Performance notes
This ticket owns the epic's performance evidence. Budgets: guard <=5 ms p95; preview <=300 ms p95 at 5 accounts; fan-out backend overhead <=50 ms + <=10 ms/account p95; WS `trade_groups` 100 ms throttle sustained; profile save <=2 s including revalidation.

## Observability
The runs validate that the metrics the stories promise actually exist and are usable: `cv_sizer_duration_seconds`, `cv_risk_guard_seconds`, `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total`, `cv_tradegroup_preview_seconds`. A missing or unusable metric is filed as a Bug against the owning ticket, because an unmeasurable budget is an unenforceable one.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.

- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

## Dependencies

title: Audit accessibility and run exploratory charters across the six profile and group screens
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus manual screen-reader passes, and the R3 a11y gate is explicit about keyboard operability of trading surfaces. E28's two grids are the hard cases: SCR-133's virtualised accounts x ~400 symbols matrix of checkboxes, and SCR-062's virtualised group grid with nested per-leg tables. E28-D05 specified how these should behave; this ticket verifies that the built code does.

Alongside the audit, the epic's exploratory charters from E28-Q01 are executed - scripted tests confirm what was anticipated, exploratory sessions find what was not.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated scans on SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and SCR-061-preview, in both themes, in every reachable state, wired as a CI check.
- Manual screen-reader passes with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS covering: matrix cell names combining account and symbol; the denied-and-locked cell's reason; bulk action names and their scope; the readiness strip's live-region announcement; the preview table's row statuses and exclusion reasons; the send button's account count; disabled-control reasons including "capped by profile"; the safety notice's non-removable framing; and the step-up dialog's focus trap and return focus.
- Keyboard-only completion of every task in the epic: create a profile, apply a template, bulk-edit the matrix, create a group, produce a preview, apply and reset an override - with zero mouse use and no keyboard traps.
- Focus-preservation verification under live updates: with a WS-driven readiness change and a preview refresh in flight, focus must not move - tested deliberately, since it is the failure mode most likely to ship.
- Text scaling at 200% and zoom at 125% on both grids, with screenshots.
- Contrast verification on the built screens in both themes against the E28-D05 measurements.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` verification.
- Execution of the four exploratory charters from E28-Q01, 90 minutes each, with session notes, and an additional charter "profiles and groups with a screen reader" run by a QA engineer experienced with assistive technology.
- Findings filed with severity and an owner; Critical and High findings fixed inside the epic.

## Out of scope
Design conformance review (E28-D07); functional regression (E28-Q05); load and chaos (E28-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
- axe-core is clean (zero violations at serious or critical severity) on all six surfaces in both themes in every reachable state, and the scan runs in CI.
- Manual screen-reader passes completed on both NVDA and VoiceOver, with notes per surface.
- Every task in the epic is completable keyboard-only, evidenced by a recording, with no traps.
- Focus is verifiably preserved across a WS update and a preview refresh.
- 200% text scaling and 125% zoom leave both grids usable, evidenced by screenshots.
- All five exploratory charters executed with session notes and a debrief.
- No Critical or High a11y finding remains open at epic close; Medium and Low findings are filed with owners.

## Technical notes / design
Virtualised grids are the audit's centre of gravity: a screen reader must report a sane row and column count, and navigating beyond the rendered window must load and announce correctly rather than silently ending the table. Both are explicitly tested against the approach E28-D05 chose.

The preview surface is audited while actively updating, not in a frozen state, because the announcement-rate cap and the focus-preservation rule can only fail under motion.

## Test plan
This ticket is the audit. Evidence: axe reports per screen and state, screen-reader session recordings, keyboard-only task recordings, zoom and scaling screenshots, contrast measurements and exploratory session notes - all attached.

## Security notes
The audit confirms that accessible paths do not weaken safety controls: the step-up prompt is a real gate for keyboard and screen-reader users; the typed acknowledgement for an aggressive template on a live account is not reducible to a single keypress; and the native-SL floor is announced as immutable policy rather than as a control that might be enabled with more permissions. Any accessible bypass of a control is a security finding and is escalated to E28-X02.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility verification for the epic and covers WCAG 2.2 AA including 2.4.11 focus appearance, 2.5.8 target size, 3.2.6 consistent help and 3.3.7 redundant entry - the last being relevant to the repeated step-up prompts across profile, template and matrix saves.

## Performance notes
Screen-reader performance on the virtualised matrix is itself a finding class: if navigating the grid with a screen reader is unusably slow at ~400 columns, that is filed as a P1 even when the visual render meets its 600 ms budget.

## Observability
Findings are tracked in the QA dashboard by severity and surface; the axe-core CI check publishes its violation count as a trend so a slow regression is visible before it becomes a gate failure.

- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.

title: Assemble the E28 regression pack and record QA sign-off for the epic
body:
## Context
The Epic DoD requires "QA sign-off: an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA". E28 is also the epic that every later trading epic builds on: E30, E34, E35, E39 and E41 all consume its profiles, its sizer and its groups. A regression pack that outlives this epic is therefore worth more than the sign-off itself - it is the net that catches E34 or E35 quietly changing a sized quantity.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Regression pack at `qa/regression/e28/` selecting the highest-value cases from E28-Q01's plan: the safety invariants (native SL cannot be disabled by any path; a non-allowed symbol is refused by the API; every risk cap holds; an override cannot widen a cap), the ten independently-recomputed golden sizing vectors, the group guards (mixed environment, empty intersection, minimum one member), and the preview's read-only property.
- Tagging of these cases so they run on every change to `candleviewer/profiles`, `candleviewer/oms/groups` and the consuming epics' paths - not only inside E28.
- A full epic-level regression run against the R3 staging build with all E28 stories merged, executed end to end with results recorded per case.
- Cross-epic smoke: confirm that a profile change is reflected in the order path (E29), in the preview, and in the audit browser (E42 when available), so the epic's contract holds outside its own boundary.
- Defect triage summary: every defect found during the epic with its status; a written statement that no P0 or P1 remains open against E28's scope.
- Consolidation of results from E28-Q02 (E2E), E28-Q03 (perf and chaos), E28-Q04 (a11y and exploratory) and E28-X03 (abuse cases) into one epic report.
- Residual-risk statement naming what was not tested and why, with each item either accepted by the Owner or turned into a follow-up ticket.
- The QA sign-off comment on the epic ticket.

## Out of scope
New feature testing (covered by the earlier Q tickets); the R3 train-level soak `q09` and the PRR (`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`).

## Acceptance criteria
- The regression pack exists, runs green against the staging build, and completes within 20 minutes so it is cheap enough to run often.
- The safety cases are tagged to run on changes in the consuming epics' paths, and that wiring is demonstrated by a deliberate trial run from an E34 branch.
- The full epic-level run is executed with per-case results recorded.
- Cross-epic smoke passes for the profile-change-to-order-path contract.
- Zero P0 or P1 defects remain open against E28's scope, stated explicitly.
- The consolidated report exists and is linked from the epic; the residual-risk statement is accepted by the Owner.
- The QA sign-off comment is posted on the epic.

## Technical notes / design
Selection criterion for the pack is blast radius, not coverage percentage: a case earns its place if its failure would produce a wrongly-sized or unprotected order. Cases that merely confirm UI text are left in the E2E suite and out of the regression pack, so the pack stays fast enough to run on unrelated changes.

The golden vectors are included by value, not by reference to the engineering fixture, so a change to the engineering fixture cannot silently change the expected answer - a divergence fails the pack loudly.

## Test plan
The pack is the test. Its health is measured by runtime and flake rate; a case that flakes is fixed or removed, never retried, because a flaky safety test is worse than no safety test - it trains people to ignore a red.

## Security notes
The pack includes the four abuse cases from E28-X03 that map to SR-052, SR-053, SR-054 and SR-056, so the security controls are re-verified on every subsequent change to the sizing and fan-out paths rather than only once at review time. The residual-risk statement is co-signed by the Security engineer where a security control is not fully automated.

## Accessibility notes
The pack includes the axe-core scan on the six surfaces so an a11y regression from a later epic is caught; the deeper manual passes remain in E28-Q04 and are re-run per release rather than per change.

## Performance notes
The pack includes the guard and preview micro-benchmarks with their regression thresholds, so a performance regression introduced by a consuming epic fails there rather than in a release gate.

## Observability

title: Produce the STRIDE threat model for per-account profiles and trade groups
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` already classifies this epic's two assets: **A-08** per-account profiles (Postgres `account_profiles`, confidentiality 2, integrity 3, availability 2 - "Tampering escalates position size / bypasses risk caps") and **A-09** trade-group / fan-out configuration ("Silently routing orders to an account the actor may not trade"). It also records the relevant threats: **O3** (quantity/price/leverage manipulated beyond profile caps, High), **F2** (per-account profile ignored so one account gets another's sizing, High), **F6** (a leg placed without a native SL because the profile lacked offsets, High) and **R2** (a rule edited to enlarge size, High).

The Epic DoR requires a STRIDE kickoff for any epic touching the OMS or fan-out, and the Epic DoD requires the model finalised with findings triaged. This ticket produces it **before** the schema is frozen, so a finding can still change a column or a constraint rather than requiring a migration later - which is why E28-T01 declares it as a blocker.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE model at `docs/security/e28/threat-model.md` covering: the profile CRUD surface, the sizing path, the risk-guard path, the group definition surface, the preview endpoint, the override surface and the `trade_groups` WS projection.
- Data-flow diagrams (mermaid) for: profile save (client -> API -> validator -> Postgres -> audit), order sizing (intent -> profile cache -> sizer -> guard -> OMS), and group preview (client -> planner -> profiles + wallets + instruments -> response).
- Threat enumeration per element with STRIDE categories, existing controls, residual risk and a proposed mitigation where residual risk is not Low - extending, not duplicating, the entries already in `04-security-program.md` SS5.3 and SS5.4.
- Specific analysis of six questions this epic raises: (1) can a manager widen their own effective caps through any path, including templates, the matrix, overrides and the group editor; (2) can a preview leak the existence, sizing or equity of an ungranted account; (3) can a profile edit retroactively change an already-open position's attribution; (4) can a group be constructed that spans environments through a subsequent account edit rather than at creation; (5) can the in-memory risk counters be desynchronised to reopen a breached cap; (6) can `profile_snapshot` ever contain secret material.
- Control mapping: every SR-* control this epic implements (SR-025, SR-052, SR-053, SR-054, SR-056, SR-064, SR-072) mapped to the ticket and the automated test that proves it, so no control is implemented-but-unproven.
- Abuse-case list handed to E28-X03 for automation, aligned with E28-Q01's hostile catalogue so the two are one list rather than two.
- Findings triaged with severity and an owner; anything Critical or High that affects the schema is raised before E28-T01 merges.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk is found.

## Out of scope
Implementing mitigations (the owning engineering tickets); the security review of the built code (E28-X02); the RBAC assertion matrix (E28-X03); pen-testing (**E43**).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every element of the three data-flow diagrams has all six STRIDE categories considered, with an explicit "not applicable" and reason where one does not apply - no silent omissions.
- The six specific questions each have a written answer with evidence, and any "yes" has a mitigation with an owner and a ticket.
- Every SR-* control in scope maps to a ticket and a named test.
- Findings are triaged with severity; Critical and High findings affecting the schema are raised before E28-T01 merges, evidenced by a comment on that ticket.
- The abuse-case list is handed over and acknowledged by E28-X03 and E28-Q01.
- Reviewed with the Architect and the Owner; the risk register is updated.

## Technical notes / design
The model pays special attention to *indirect* widening paths, because the direct one (edit the cap) is obviously controlled. Indirect paths worth enumerating: a template that carries a wider cap; a matrix bulk action that empties an allow-list and thereby permits everything; an override that appears to narrow one field while widening another; a group edit that adds an account whose profile is wider; and a profile clone that copies caps across environments.

Question 5 (counter desynchronisation) is analysed jointly with E28-Q03's chaos scenarios so the analysis and the test are designed together.

## Test plan
Not a code ticket. The model's rigour is verified by the review with the Architect and the Owner, and by the completeness check that every element x every STRIDE category has a written disposition.

## Security notes
This ticket is security work. Its own handling rules: the document is Internal, contains no real credentials or account identifiers, and lives under `docs/security/e28/` with the rest of the programme's artefacts.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - a document. One finding class is in scope, though: an accessible path that bypasses a control (for example a keyboard shortcut that skips step-up) is a security finding, and the model states that explicitly so E28-Q04 knows to escalate rather than merely file.

## Performance notes
Where a control has a performance cost the model records it, so a later optimisation cannot silently remove a control - specifically the <=5 ms guard budget, which must not be met by skipping gates.

## Observability
The model names the audit events that constitute the evidence trail for each threat (`profile.updated`, `order.refused_by_profile`, `tradegroup.row_overridden`, `symbol_permission.change_refused`) and requires that each is emitted at the point of decision, not after the fact.

- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets-scan clean or triaged on the branches this ticket touches.

title: Security-review the sizing, risk-guard and override implementation against its threat model
body:
## Context
E28-X01 modelled the threats; this ticket verifies the built code closes them. The three modules under review are the ones an attacker would target: the sizer (E28-T03), which decides how large every order is; the risk guard (E28-T04), which is the only thing standing between a hostile client and an unbounded position; and the override path (E28-S05), which by design permits a deviation from policy and must permit only a narrowing one.

The R3 security gate requires "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes", and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` holds the security-relevant modules to >=90% coverage.

## Scope / Deliverables
- White-box review of `candleviewer/profiles/` (validator, sizer, guard, repository) and `candleviewer/oms/groups/` (group definition, planner, preview), with findings recorded per file and function.
- Verification that each control does what its SR-* entry claims:
  - **SR-052** - no code path accepts a client-supplied size, leverage or cap as authoritative; every one is re-derived. Verified by reading every call site of the sizer and the guard, not only their definitions.
  - **SR-053** - hard notional and leverage ceilings cannot be exceeded by any combination of profile, template, override and group membership.
  - **SR-054** - the allow-list is applied on every order path including rule-originated orders, with wildcard expansion that cannot be tricked into matching an unlisted symbol.
  - **SR-056** - no path can produce a profile without a stop definition, and the database CHECK remains in place in the merged migration.
  - **SR-025** - step-up is enforced server-side on every profile, template and matrix write, not only in the UI.
  - **SR-064/SR-072** - every refusal, clamp and group edit produces an audit row at the point of decision.
- Fail-closed verification: every error path in the guard is traced to confirm it refuses rather than permits, including exception paths, and that no `except` swallows a failure into a permit.
- Confirmation that `profile_snapshot` and every API response are free of secret material, by a serialisation test over the full model rather than by inspection.
- Review of the override decision table against the safety floor, field by field, with `require_native_sl`, the allowed-symbol set and each hard cap confirmed `never`.
- Review of the preview endpoint's read-only property and its rate limit as an abuse-amplification control.
- SAST results (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) for the epic's paths triaged, with any suppression justified in writing.
- Findings filed with severity and an owner; Critical and High closed before the epic closes.
- Security sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
The threat model itself (E28-X01); automated abuse-case tests (E28-X03 - this review specifies them, X03 automates them); pen-testing (**E43**).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every module in scope is reviewed with findings recorded per file, and the review is evidenced by a written report, not only by a PR approval.
- Each of SR-025, SR-052, SR-053, SR-054, SR-056, SR-064 and SR-072 has a written verdict with the evidence that supports it, including the test that proves it.
- Fail-closed behaviour is confirmed on every error path in the guard, including exception paths, with the traced paths listed.
- The no-secrets property of `profile_snapshot` and of every profile and group API response is proven by a test, not asserted.
- The override decision table is confirmed against the safety floor field by field.
- SAST is clean or every finding is triaged with a justified disposition.
- No Critical or High finding remains open; the security sign-off comment is posted.

## Technical notes / design
The review deliberately reads **call sites** rather than definitions for SR-052: a correct sizer that some caller bypasses is worth nothing, and bypass is the realistic failure mode once E30, E34 and E35 start consuming this code. The reviewer enumerates every import of the sizer and the guard across the repository and checks each one.

Wildcard expansion is reviewed as a parsing problem: a pattern like `*USDT` must not be implemented with a substring check that would also match a symbol containing "USDT" in the middle, and must not permit a pattern that expands to something outside the listed linear USDT-perp universe.

## Test plan
The review's findings become tests in E28-X03 and in the owning tickets. The no-secrets and fail-closed properties are landed as tests in this ticket's own PR so they cannot regress, even though the rest of the ticket is a review.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification for the epic. Conflict-of-interest rule: the reviewer is the Security engineer, not an author of the code under review. Findings are tracked in `docs/security/e28/review.md` with severity, owner and status; accepted risks carry an Owner signature and an expiry date.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except that any accessible bypass of a control reported by E28-Q04 is triaged here as a security finding rather than an a11y one.

## Performance notes
The review confirms that the <=5 ms guard budget is met by efficiency (caching, ordering) rather than by omitting gates - a gate order change that short-circuits a control for speed is a finding.

## Observability
The review confirms that every refusal, clamp and denied attempt produces an audit row at the point of decision, and that audit emission cannot be skipped by an early return - the realistic way an audit trail silently develops holes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Deliverable committed under `docs/security/e28/` and cross-linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding closed or accepted-risk with a written Owner sign-off and an expiry date.

title: Automate the abuse-case and RBAC assertion suite for every profile and trade-group route
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion #10 is unambiguous: "RBAC: an automated matrix test exercises **every** route x every role and asserts 403 + no state change + audit row for every disallowed combination." E28 adds seven REST routes and one WS topic to that matrix. US-PROF-003's second scenario is itself an abuse case ("a crafted request submits a DOGEUSDT order for account B / the server rejects with 403 and audits the attempt"), and US-PROF-004 exists entirely so that "limits survive a broken or hostile client".

A one-off manual check does not satisfy this; the assertions must be a suite that runs on every change, because the controls' value is that they hold in six months when E34 and E35 are modifying the same paths.

## Scope / Deliverables
- RBAC matrix test at `tests/security/e28/test_rbac_matrix.py` covering every E28 route x every role and scope: `GET`/`POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles/{profileId}`, `GET`/`POST /trade-groups`, `GET /trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}`, `POST /trade-groups/preview`, and the `trade_groups` WS topic - against owner, manager-with-grant, manager-without-grant, viewer and unauthenticated.
- For every disallowed cell the test asserts all three properties, not just the status: 403 (or the documented `account_scope_denied`), **no state change** (verified by a before/after snapshot of the affected tables), and an **audit row** recording the denied attempt.
- Abuse-case suite implementing the list from E28-X01 and E28-Q01:
  1. `require_native_sl = false` attempted through create, update, template apply and a raw payload - all refused with `native_stop_mandatory` and audited.
  2. An order for a non-allowed symbol via the API directly, bypassing the UI - 403, no exchange call, audited.
  3. An oversized quantity hint on preview and submit - clamped to the profile's computation, clamp recorded.
  4. An override widening each protected cap in turn (`max_position_notional`, `max_daily_loss`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage_cap`, the allow-list, `require_native_sl`) - each clamped or refused and audited.
  5. A group mixing demo and live accounts, and a group edited after creation to span environments - both refused.
  6. A preview requested for an ungranted account, and a group read whose membership includes an ungranted account - neither leaks sizing, equity or existence.
  7. A profile write without step-up - refused with `step_up_required` and audited.
  8. A wildcard allow-list pattern crafted to match an unlisted or non-USDT-perp symbol - refused.
  9. Idempotency-key reuse with a different body - `409 idempotency_key_reuse`.
  10. A crafted `profile_snapshot` supplied by the client on a submit - ignored; the server's own snapshot is used.
- WS scope assertions: a subscription requesting `exchange_account_ids` beyond the caller's grants is silently narrowed, never errored and never echoed back, and no frame for an ungranted account is ever delivered.
- Wiring into CI as a **required check** on the E28 paths, so a regression blocks merge rather than release.
- A short report mapping each abuse case to the SR-* control and the threat id it defends.

## Out of scope
The threat model (E28-X01) and the manual review (E28-X02); fan-out submission abuse cases (**E34**); pen-testing (**E43**).

## Acceptance criteria
- The RBAC matrix covers every E28 route and the WS topic x every role, with no cell untested; a coverage report proves it.
- Every disallowed cell asserts 403, no state change and an audit row - all three, with the state-change assertion implemented as a real table snapshot diff.
- All ten abuse cases are automated and pass, each asserting the refusal or clamp **and** its audit row.
- The WS scope-narrowing behaviour is asserted, including that denied ids are not echoed back.
- The suite is a required CI check on the E28 paths and runs in under 5 minutes.
- The report maps each case to its SR-* control and threat id and is reviewed by the Security engineer.

## Technical notes / design
The "no state change" assertion is the one usually skipped and the one that matters: a route that returns 403 after writing a row is still a breach. It is implemented as a checksum over the affected tables taken before and after each disallowed call, so it catches a write the test author did not anticipate.

Audit assertions query the audit chain by correlation id rather than by scanning, so the test fails on a missing row rather than on a slow one, and does not become flaky as the audit table grows.

The suite runs against a seeded fixture (shared with E28-Q01) with deterministic role grants, so adding a role or a route surfaces as an explicit test failure - the matrix is generated from the route table and the role list, so a new route without a matrix entry fails the coverage check automatically.

## Test plan
The suite is the test. Its own correctness is verified by mutation-style checks: temporarily removing a control in a scratch branch must make the corresponding case fail, and this is demonstrated once per control at review time and recorded, so the suite is proven to actually detect the breach it claims to.

## Security notes
This ticket automates controls SR-025, SR-052, SR-053, SR-054, SR-056, SR-064 and the RBAC requirements of SR-070..SR-074, and defends threats O3, F2, F4 and F6 from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Fixtures use non-functional synthetic keys and demo-only accounts. The suite must never be run against a live UID, enforced by an environment guard that aborts the run if the target configuration is live.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - API-level tests.

## Performance notes
The suite runs in under 5 minutes so it can be a required check on every PR; the RBAC matrix is parallelised by route.

## Observability
The suite asserts on audit rows, which makes it a continuous verification that the epic's observability actually works - a silently broken audit pipeline fails these tests rather than being discovered during an incident.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Deliverable committed under `docs/security/e28/` and cross-linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

title: Run the cap-bypass and privilege-escalation drills and record the E28 security sign-off
body:
## Context
Automated suites prove the controls that were thought of. A drill is where a person tries to get around them with the system in front of them, which is how the R3 gate phrases it: "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes". This ticket runs the drills for E28's two assets and records the epic's security sign-off, which the Epic DoD requires.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Drill 1 - **cap bypass**: with a manager account granted one demo account, attempt to place an order larger than the profile permits by every available path: the UI, the REST API directly, a per-row override, a template applied to widen caps, a bulk symbol change, a group whose other members are wider, a replayed idempotency key, and a concurrent edit race between a profile widening and an order submit. Each attempt is recorded with its outcome and its audit trail.
- Drill 2 - **privilege escalation**: attempt to read or act on an ungranted account through the profile routes, the group routes, the preview endpoint and the WS topic, including by guessing identifiers, by supplying an ungranted id in a list parameter, and by subscribing with a broad `exchange_account_ids` set.
- Drill 3 - **counter desynchronisation**: with a cap breached, attempt to clear it by forcing a restart, a WS reconnect and a clock change, in coordination with E28-Q03's chaos scenarios; confirm the cap survives all three.
- Drill 4 - **native-SL invariant**: attempt to create or use a profile that yields an order without a stop, by every path including the templates and the override surface; confirm every attempt is refused and audited. This is a rehearsal for R3 exit criterion #2, which will be run train-wide.
- For each drill: a written outcome, the audit evidence, and a finding if any attempt succeeded or was not audited.
- Verification that every attempt - successful or not - left an audit row, since an unaudited failed attempt is itself a finding.
- Consolidated security report at `docs/security/e28/signoff.md` with the control verdicts from E28-X02, the suite results from E28-X03 and these drill outcomes.
- Risk-register update and the security sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission drills (**E34**); the key-compromise drills (**E27-X04**); pen-testing (**E43**); the R3 train-wide safety-invariant suite (run at the train gate).

## Acceptance criteria
- All four drills executed with written outcomes and audit evidence attached.
- Every attempt, successful or not, is shown to have produced an audit row; a missing row is filed as a finding regardless of whether the attempt succeeded.
- Any successful bypass is a P0 finding, fixed and re-drilled before the epic closes - not accepted as a risk.
- The consolidated report exists, links E28-X02 and E28-X03 results, and states a verdict per SR-* control in scope.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated with anything found or retired.
- The security sign-off comment is posted on the epic by the Security engineer.

## Technical notes / design
Drills run on the R3 demo staging environment with the E28-Q01 fixtures and a manager account created for the purpose. The drill operator is the Security engineer, working from the system as a user would - not from the code - so that a control which exists but is unreachable through a real path is discovered.

Drill 1's concurrent-edit race is the subtlest case: a profile widened between the guard's read and the order's submission could, with an unlucky cache design, permit an order neither version would allow. It is executed deliberately with timing control, because it is unlikely to be found by chance.

## Test plan
Drills are manual by design. Anything a drill finds that can be automated is added to E28-X03's suite before the epic closes, so the same gap cannot reopen silently.

## Security notes
This ticket is the epic's final security gate. Its report is an input to the R3 PRR (`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`) and to **E43**'s pen-test scoping - the drills' findings tell the pen-testers where this system is weakest, so the report is shared with them rather than filed away. All drills are demo-only; an environment guard is verified before each run.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except that drill 2 includes attempting a control bypass via keyboard-only paths and via any skip-link or shortcut, since an accessible shortcut that skips a confirmation is a real escalation path.

## Performance notes
N/A - though drill 3 is coordinated with E28-Q03 so the restart and reconnect measurements are taken once and used by both.

## Observability
Drills double as a verification that the audit trail is complete and usable under adversarial conditions: the Security engineer must be able to reconstruct every attempt from the audit browser alone, without database access. If they cannot, that is a finding against the observability of the epic.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Deliverable committed under `docs/security/e28/` and cross-linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding closed or accepted-risk with a written Owner sign-off and an expiry date.
- [ ] Applicable SR-* controls from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mapped to an automated test (unit, contract, integration or e2e) so the control cannot silently regress.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets-scan clean or triaged on the branches this ticket touches.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-X02** (review verdicts), **E28-X03** (the automated suite the drills complement) and **E28-S05** (the override surface drill 1 probes). Coordinates with **E28-Q03** on chaos scenarios. Its sign-off is required by the epic DoD and feeds the R3 PRR.
